    Methods for fitted models¶

    Functions that take a fitted model. Each is a single-dispatch function: the generic function chooses the implementation from the class of the fitted model, and the implementations are documented below the generic. A call with a class that has no implementation raises metafopy.errors.ArgumentError.

    Predictions and intervals¶

    predict ¶

    predict(
    model: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any
) -> PredictResult

    Predicted values for a fitted model, with confidence and prediction intervals (metafor's predict.rma).

    This is a single-dispatch function: the implementation is chosen by the class of model. See predict_rma_uni, predict_rma_glmm, predict_rma_mv and predict_rma_ls for the arguments of each. The fits of rma_mh and rma_peto (predict_fixed_binary, the arguments of predict_rma_uni; newmods is not accepted), of selmodel and the results of matreg are also registered.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model Any

    The fitted model. Its class selects the implementation.

    		 required
    *args Any

    Positional arguments passed on to the implementation (newmods first).

    		 ()
    **kwargs Any

    Keyword arguments passed on to the implementation.

    		 {}

    Returns:

    Type Description
    PredictResult

    The predictions, a PredictResult.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ArgumentError

    there is no implementation for the class of model. An argument the implementation does not have is a TypeError from Python, as for any function.

    predict_rma_uni ¶

    predict_rma_uni(
    model: RMAResult,
    newmods: ArrayLike
    | Mapping[str, float]
    | Series
    | DataFrame
    | PairmatSpec
    | None = None,
    *,
    intercept: bool | None = None,
    tau2_levels: Sequence[str | int]
    | str
    | int
    | None = None,
    gamma2_levels: Sequence[str | int]
    | str
    | int
    | None = None,
    hetvar: ArrayLike | None = None,
    prob: str | float | None = None,
    addx: bool = False,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    level: float | None = None,
    adjust: bool = False,
    vcov: bool = False,
    predtype: str | None = None,
    pi_type: str | None = None,
    newvi: ArrayLike | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    digits: int | Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> PredictResult

    Predicted values, standard errors, confidence intervals and prediction intervals for an rma_uni fit.

    Without newmods an intercept-only model gives the pooled estimate and a meta-regression the fitted value of each study.

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/predict.rma.r

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model RMAResult

    Model fitted by rma_uni.

    		 required
    newmods ArrayLike | Mapping[str, float] | Series | DataFrame | PairmatSpec | None

    Moderator values of new studies to predict for, without the intercept column (it is added, see intercept) or with all p columns (then intercept is ignored, with a warning if given, and the first column decides whether the intercept is included). A number or 1-d array gives one prediction per value if the model has a single moderator and one prediction otherwise; a 2-d array gives one prediction per row. A dict, pandas Series or DataFrame with string names is matched by name to the moderators of the model when it has more than one moderator (a name may be shortened to any subsequence of the moderator name, as in metafor). The predictions are labelled by the index of a DataFrame with string index, or by the names of a dict or Series for a model with a single moderator, else by their position. A pairmat specification is also accepted. Factors must be given as the contrast variables of the model matrix. Models without moderators do not accept newmods. Default: no new values, so an intercept-only model gives the pooled estimate and a meta-regression the fitted value of every study.

    		 None
    intercept bool | None

    Whether to include the intercept when predicting for newmods: if False, the intercept column is set to 0. Default: the column of ones is added if the model has an intercept. Ignored when newmods has all p columns.

    		 None
    tau2_levels Sequence[str | int] | str | int | None

    Levels of the inner factor for the prediction interval. Accepted for compatibility with metafor; it has no effect for this model.

    		 None
    gamma2_levels Sequence[str | int] | str | int | None

    Levels of the inner factor for the prediction interval. Accepted for compatibility with metafor; it has no effect for this model.

    		 None
    hetvar ArrayLike | None

    Amount of heterogeneity to use in the prediction interval instead of the estimated tau^2: a number or one value per prediction (a different length raises InputError). Default: the estimate of the model.

    		 None
    prob str | float | None

    Probability to add to the result, as a string such as '>0.2' or '<0': the probability that a true outcome is above (>) or below (<) the cutoff, from the predictive distribution (normal or t, see predtype). A number means >. The cutoff may be an arithmetic expression (+ - * / ^) using the constants pi and Inf and the functions abs, atanh, cos, exp, log, log10, log1p, log2, plogis, qlogis, sin, sqrt, tan and tanh, such as '>log(0.8)'; a string that is not such an expression gives no prob, as in metafor. Cannot be combined with adjust=True. Default: none.

    		 None
    addx bool

    Add the model matrix of the predictions to the result (X).

    		 False
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to each predicted value and interval bound separately (for example numpy.exp); se is then NaN and the lower and upper bounds are put in order. Default: no transformation.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Second argument passed to transf (transf(value, targs)). Default: none, except for the integral and mode transformations of transf, which get {'tau2': tau2}.

    		 None
    level float | None

    Confidence and prediction interval level in percent (95 is 95%). As in metafor, a value below 1 is read as the confidence level if it is above 0.5 (0.95) and as the significance level otherwise (0.05). Default: the level of the model.

    		 None
    adjust bool

    Apply a Bonferroni correction: the significance level is divided by the number of predictions, which widens the intervals.

    		 False
    vcov bool

    Add the variance-covariance matrix of the predictions to the result (vcov; metafor returns it as a second list element). Ignored with transf.

    		 False
    predtype str | None

    Type of prediction interval: 'default' (the normal distribution, or the t distribution with the degrees of freedom ddf of the test), 'simple' (ignore the uncertainty of the predicted value, normal distribution), 'riley' (t distribution with ddf - parms + p degrees of freedom, which is k - parms when ddf = k - p; Riley et al., 2011, doi:10.1136/bmj.d549) or 't' (t distribution with ddf degrees of freedom); degrees of freedom below 1 are set to 1. Case is ignored and a unique prefix is accepted. Default: pi_type, else 'default'.

    		 None
    pi_type str | None

    Old spelling of predtype, used when predtype is None.

    		 None
    newvi ArrayLike | None

    Sampling variances of the new studies, added to the variance of the prediction interval: a number or one value per prediction (a different length raises InputError). Default: 0.

    		 None
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    What to do with studies left out of the fit because of missing values: 'omit', 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail' (metafor takes this from the na.action option). For the fitted values (no newmods) of a meta-regression, 'omit' returns the studies used in fitting, 'exclude' one row per study with NaN for those left out and 'pass' one row per study computed from the moderator values it has. 'fail' raises if any study was left out of the fit, also when newmods is given. Predictions for newmods drop ('omit') or keep ('exclude', 'pass') the rows that are NaN.

    		 'omit'
    digits int | Mapping[str, int] | None

    Number of decimals used when printing, or a mapping with any of the keys est, se, test, pval, ci, var, sevar, fit and het (a unique prefix of a key is accepted). It is stored in the result and does not change the values. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

    		 None
    verbose bool

    Accepted for metafor's printing of the details of a failing clubSandwich contrast; it has no effect here.

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    PredictResult

    The predictions, a PredictResult with pred, se, ci_lb, ci_ub, pi_lb and pi_ub (one entry per
    PredictResult

    prediction; the prediction interval is NaN where there is none), plus prob, X and vcov if requested. Unlike metafor, vcov is a
    PredictResult

    field of the result, not a second list element.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    an argument or the data is invalid (for example prob with adjust=True, newmods of the wrong width or for a model without moderators, an unknown predtype or na_action, a hetvar or newvi of the wrong length, or a fit made robust with club_sandwich=True and the saddlepoint test).
    Metafor reference

    predict.rma

    predict_rma_glmm ¶

    predict_rma_glmm(
    model: GLMMResult,
    newmods: ArrayLike
    | Mapping[str, float]
    | Series
    | DataFrame
    | PairmatSpec
    | None = None,
    *,
    intercept: bool | None = None,
    tau2_levels: Sequence[str | int]
    | str
    | int
    | None = None,
    gamma2_levels: Sequence[str | int]
    | str
    | int
    | None = None,
    hetvar: ArrayLike | None = None,
    prob: str | float | None = None,
    addx: bool = False,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    level: float | None = None,
    adjust: bool = False,
    vcov: bool = False,
    predtype: str | None = None,
    pi_type: str | None = None,
    newvi: ArrayLike | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    digits: int | Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> PredictResult

    Predicted values for an rma_glmm fit (metafor's predict.rma; the arguments are those of predict_rma_uni).

    The predictions are on the scale of the linear predictor of the model: with the default links, log odds ratios (measure='OR'), log incidence rate ratios ('IRR'), log odds ('PLO') or log incidence rates ('IRLN'); the experimental measures and a different link change the scale. Without newmods a meta-regression gives the fitted value of each study that entered the model. Prediction intervals add tau2 and are absent (NaN) for the fixed-effects methods.

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/predict.rma.r

    Name Type Description Default

    Model fitted by rma_glmm.

    predict_rma_mv(
    model: RMAMVResult,
    newmods: ArrayLike
    | Mapping[str, float]

    *,

    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    level: float | None = None,
    adjust: bool = False,
    vcov: bool = False,
    predtype: str | None = None,
    pi_type: str | None = None,
    newvi: ArrayLike | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    digits: int | Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> PredictResult

    Predicted values for an rma_mv fit (metafor's predict.rma; the arguments are those of predict_rma_uni unless stated).

    Prediction intervals add the sum of the sigma2 values and, when present, the tau2 and gamma2 values selected via tau2_levels and gamma2_levels. They are NaN when several tau2 or gamma2 values exist and no levels are given. A model without moderators cannot be given newmods. For the fitted values of studies left out of the fit (na_action='pass'), the tau2 and gamma2 value of a study whose inner level is lost is NaN when the model has several of them.

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/predict.rma.r

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model RMAMVResult

    Model fitted by rma_mv.

    		 required
    newmods ArrayLike | Mapping[str, float] | Series | DataFrame | PairmatSpec | None

    Moderator values of new studies to predict for, without the intercept column (it is added, see intercept) or with all p columns (then intercept is ignored, with a warning if given, and the first column decides whether the intercept is included). A number or 1-d array gives one prediction per value if the model has a single moderator and one prediction otherwise; a 2-d array gives one prediction per row. A dict, pandas Series or DataFrame with string names is matched by name to the moderators of the model when it has more than one moderator (a name may be shortened to any subsequence of the moderator name, as in metafor). The predictions are labelled by the index of a DataFrame with string index, or by the names of a dict or Series for a model with a single moderator, else by their position. A pairmat specification is also accepted. Factors must be given as the contrast variables of the model matrix. Models without moderators do not accept newmods. Default: no new values, so an intercept-only model gives the pooled estimate and a meta-regression the fitted value of every study.

    		 None
    intercept bool | None

    Whether to include the intercept when predicting for newmods: if False, the intercept column is set to 0. Default: the column of ones is added if the model has an intercept. Ignored when newmods has all p columns.

    		 None
    tau2_levels Sequence[str | int] | str | int | None

    Which tau2 value(s) to use in the prediction interval when the model has several: labels of the inner factor of the first inner | outer term or 0-based positions (a single value, used for every prediction, or a sequence with one per prediction). Default: none. With newmods and several tau2 values the prediction intervals are then NaN (metafor requires the levels). With the fitted values of a meta-regression the levels are those of the studies and tau2_levels is ignored (with a warning). For an intercept-only model metafor then returns one prediction for each tau2 value, whereas metafopy returns a single prediction with a NaN prediction interval.

    		 None
    gamma2_levels Sequence[str | int] | str | int | None

    As tau2_levels, for the gamma2 values (second inner | outer term).

    		 None
    hetvar ArrayLike | None

    Amount of heterogeneity to use in the prediction interval instead of the sum of the variance components: a number or one value per prediction (a different length raises InputError). tau2_levels and gamma2_levels are then ignored (with a warning).

    		 None
    prob str | float | None

    Probability to add to the result, as a string such as '>0.2' or '<0': the probability that a true outcome is above (>) or below (<) the cutoff, from the predictive distribution (normal or t, see predtype). A number means >. The cutoff may be an arithmetic expression (+ - * / ^) using the constants pi and Inf and the functions abs, atanh, cos, exp, log, log10, log1p, log2, plogis, qlogis, sin, sqrt, tan and tanh, such as '>log(0.8)'; a string that is not such an expression gives no prob, as in metafor. Cannot be combined with adjust=True. Default: none.

    		 None
    addx bool

    Add the model matrix of the predictions to the result (X).

    		 False
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to each predicted value and interval bound separately (for example numpy.exp); se is then NaN and the lower and upper bounds are put in order. Default: no transformation.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Second argument passed to transf (transf(value, targs)). Default: none, except for the integral and mode transformations of transf, which get {'tau2': tau2}.

    		 None
    level float | None

    Confidence and prediction interval level in percent (95 is 95%). As in metafor, a value below 1 is read as the confidence level if it is above 0.5 (0.95) and as the significance level otherwise (0.05). Default: the level of the model.

    		 None
    adjust bool

    Apply a Bonferroni correction: the significance level is divided by the number of predictions, which widens the intervals.

    		 False
    vcov bool

    Add the variance-covariance matrix of the predictions to the result (vcov; metafor returns it as a second list element). Ignored with transf.

    		 False
    predtype str | None

    Type of prediction interval: 'default' (the normal distribution, or the t distribution with the degrees of freedom ddf of the test), 'simple' (ignore the uncertainty of the predicted value, normal distribution), 'riley' (t distribution with ddf - parms + p degrees of freedom, which is k - parms when ddf = k - p; Riley et al., 2011, doi:10.1136/bmj.d549) or 't' (t distribution with ddf degrees of freedom); degrees of freedom below 1 are set to 1. Case is ignored and a unique prefix is accepted. Default: pi_type, else 'default'.

    		 None
    pi_type str | None

    Old spelling of predtype, used when predtype is None.

    		 None
    newvi ArrayLike | None

    Sampling variances of the new studies, added to the variance of the prediction interval: a number or one value per prediction (a different length raises InputError). Default: 0.

    		 None
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    What to do with studies left out of the fit because of missing values: 'omit', 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail' (metafor takes this from the na.action option). For the fitted values (no newmods) of a meta-regression, 'omit' returns the studies used in fitting, 'exclude' one row per study with NaN for those left out and 'pass' one row per study computed from the moderator values it has. 'fail' raises if any study was left out of the fit, also when newmods is given. Predictions for newmods drop ('omit') or keep ('exclude', 'pass') the rows that are NaN.

    		 'omit'
    digits int | Mapping[str, int] | None

    Number of decimals used when printing, or a mapping with any of the keys est, se, test, pval, ci, var, sevar, fit and het (a unique prefix of a key is accepted). It is stored in the result and does not change the values. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

    		 None
    verbose bool

    Accepted for metafor's printing of the details of a failing clubSandwich contrast; it has no effect here.

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    PredictResult

    The predictions, a PredictResult with pred, se, ci_lb, ci_ub, pi_lb and pi_ub (one entry per
    PredictResult

    prediction; the prediction interval is NaN where there is none), plus prob, X and vcov if requested. Unlike metafor, vcov is a
    PredictResult

    field of the result, not a second list element.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    an argument or the data is invalid (for example newmods for a model without moderators, a level in tau2_levels or gamma2_levels that does not exist or a sequence of the wrong length, prob with adjust=True, an unknown predtype or na_action, or a hetvar or newvi of the wrong length).

    Predicted values for a location-scale model, fitted by rma_uni with scale (metafor's predict.rma.ls).

    What is predicted depends on the arguments. Without newmods and newscale the result holds the fitted values of the studies, with prediction intervals that use the tau^2 of each study. With newmods only it holds the predicted effects with confidence intervals; the prediction intervals are NaN, since tau^2 is not known for the new studies. With both it holds the predicted effects with confidence and prediction intervals, using the tau^2 predicted from newscale. With newscale only, pred holds the predicted log(tau^2) (log link) or tau^2 (identity link), pred_type is 'scale' and the prediction intervals are NaN (use transf=numpy.exp for tau^2 under the log link). With the identity link and no transf, negative predicted tau^2 values are set to 0 with a warning.

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/predict.rma.r

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model RMALSResult

    Location-scale model fitted by rma_uni with scale.

    		 required
    newmods ArrayLike | PairmatSpec | None

    Moderator values of new studies to predict for, without the intercept column (it is added, see intercept) or with all p columns (then intercept is ignored, with a warning if given). A number or 1-d array gives one prediction per value if the model has a single moderator and one prediction otherwise; a 2-d array gives one prediction per row. A dict, pandas Series or DataFrame with string names is matched by name to the moderators of the model when it has more than one moderator (a name may be shortened to any subsequence of the moderator name, as in metafor). A pairmat specification is also accepted. Factors must be given as the contrast variables of the model matrix. A model without moderators accepts only newmods=1. Default: none (the fitted values of the studies if newscale is not given either).

    		 None
    intercept bool | None

    Whether to include the intercept when predicting for newmods (and newscale if newmods is not given): if False, the intercept column is set to 0. Default: the column of ones is added if the model has an intercept. Ignored when the matrix has all its columns; the intercept column of newscale is always 1 when newmods is given too.

    		 None
    addx bool

    Add the model matrix of the predictions to the result (X).

    		 False
    newscale ArrayLike | None

    Values of the scale variables of the new studies, without the intercept column (added, see intercept) or with all q columns; same forms as newmods. A model without scale variables accepts only newscale=1. If both are given, they must have the same number of rows, except that a single row of either is repeated. Default: none (see the description).

    		 None
    addz bool

    Add the model matrix of the scale variables of the predictions to the result (Z).

    		 False
    prob str | None

    Probability to add to the result, as a string such as '>0.2' or '<0': the probability that a true outcome is above (>) or below (<) the cutoff, from the predictive distribution (normal or t, see predtype). The cutoff may be an arithmetic expression as for predict; a string that is not one gives no prob. Not computed for scale predictions (newscale only). Cannot be combined with adjust=True. Default: none.

    		 None
    level float | None

    Confidence and prediction interval level in percent (95 is 95%). As in metafor, a value below 1 is read as the confidence level if it is above 0.5 (0.95) and as the significance level otherwise (0.05). Default: the level of the model.

    		 None
    adjust bool

    Apply a Bonferroni correction: the significance level is divided by the number of predictions, which widens the intervals.

    		 False
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to each predicted value and interval bound separately (for example numpy.exp); se is then NaN and the lower and upper bounds are put in order. Default: no transformation.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Second argument passed to transf (transf(value, targs)). Default: none; unlike for predict of an rma_uni fit, the integral and mode transformations get no default tau2.

    		 None
    vcov bool

    Add the variance-covariance matrix of the predictions to the result (vcov; metafor returns it as a second list element). Ignored with transf.

    		 False
    predtype str | None

    Type of prediction interval: 'default' (the normal distribution, or the t distribution with k - p degrees of freedom if the test is 't', 'knha' or 'adhoc'), 'simple' (ignore the uncertainty of the predicted value, normal distribution), 'riley' (t distribution with k - p - q degrees of freedom, Riley et al., 2011, doi:10.1136/bmj.d549) or 't' (t distribution with k - p degrees of freedom); degrees of freedom below 1 are set to 1. Case is ignored and a unique prefix is accepted. Default: pi_type, else 'default'.

    		 None
    pi_type str | None

    Old spelling of predtype, used when predtype is None.

    		 None
    newvi ArrayLike | None

    Sampling variances of the new studies, added to the variance of the prediction interval: a number or one value per prediction. Default: 0.

    		 None
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    What to do with studies left out of the fit because of missing values: 'omit', 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail' (metafor takes this from the na.action option). For the fitted values (no newmods or newscale), 'omit' returns the studies used in fitting, 'exclude' one row per study with NaN for those left out and 'pass' one row per study computed from the values it has. 'fail' raises if any study was left out of the fit, also when newmods or newscale is given. Predictions for newmods or newscale drop ('omit') or keep ('exclude', 'pass') the rows that are NaN.

    		 'omit'
    digits int | Mapping[str, int] | None

    Number of decimals used when printing, or a mapping with any of the keys est, se, test, pval, ci, var, sevar, fit and het (a unique prefix of a key is accepted). It is stored in the result and does not change the values. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

    		 None
    verbose bool

    Accepted for compatibility with metafor; it has no effect here.

    		 False

    Type Description
    LSPredictResult

    The predictions, an LSPredictResult: a PredictResult with the extra fields Z (the scale model matrix, with
    LSPredictResult

    addz=True; None otherwise) and z_names. pred_type is 'location' or 'scale'; the predicted tau^2 of a scale prediction is
    LSPredictResult

    in pred (there is no tau2 field). ddf is a single number, None if the test is 'z'. Unlike metafor, vcov is a field of the
    LSPredictResult

    result, not a second list element.

    Confidence intervals for the coefficients and variance components of a fitted model (metafor's confint).

    This is a single-dispatch function: the implementation is chosen by the class of model. See confint_rma_uni, confint_rma_mv, confint_rma_ls and confint_fixed_binary; selection model fits (selmodel) are registered too.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model Any

    The fitted model. Its class selects the implementation.

    		 required
    *args Any

    Positional arguments passed on to the implementation.

    		 ()
    **kwargs Any

    Keyword arguments passed on to the implementation.

    		 {}

    Type Description
    Any

    The intervals, a ConfintResult (a ConfintList, a list of them, for some rma_mv, location-scale and selection
    Any

    model requests).

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ArgumentError

    there is no implementation for the class of model (for example an rma_glmm fit, as in metafor). An argument the implementation does not have is a TypeError from Python, as for any function.

    confint_rma_uni ¶

    confint_rma_uni(
    model: RMAResult,
    *,
    fixed: bool = False,
    random: bool = True,
    type: CIType | None = None,
    level: float | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    tau2_min: float | None = None,
    tau2_max: float | None = None,
    tol: float = DEFAULT_TOL,
    maxiter: int = 1000,
    verbose: bool | int = False,
    digits: int | None = None,
    control: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    xlim: float | Sequence[float] | None = None,
    extint: bool = False,
    parm: Any = None,
) -> ConfintResult

    Confidence intervals for the coefficients and for tau^2, I^2 and H^2 of an rma_uni fit (metafor's confint.rma.uni).

    The interval for tau^2 is found by root finding (Q-profile, generalised Q, profile likelihood or the Higgins-Thompson method) or is of Wald type; the bounds of I^2 and H^2 follow from those of tau^2.

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/confint.rma.uni.r

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model RMAResult

    Model fitted by rma_uni.

    		 required
    fixed bool

    Give Wald-type intervals for the coefficients (fixed table of the result), using the t distribution with the degrees of freedom of the test if the model uses it, else the normal distribution.

    		 False
    random bool

    Give intervals for tau^2 (and tau), I^2 and H^2 (random table). At least one of fixed and random must be True.

    		 True
    type CIType | None

    Method for the interval of tau^2 (case is ignored; any other value raises InputError): 'qp' (Q-profile, Viechtbauer, 2007, doi:10.1002/sim.2514; needs positive sampling variances), 'genq' (generalised Q, Jackson, 2013, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1081; needs a GENQ or GENQM fit), 'pl' (profile likelihood, which metafor suggests for ML and REML fits; the likelihood used is the REML one for method='REML' and the ML one otherwise), 'ht' (the test-based method of Higgins and Thompson, 2002, doi:10.1002/sim.1186; only for models without moderators and k > 2), or a Wald type 'wald', 'wald.log' or 'wald.sqrt' (in the metafor source but not described on its reference page). Default: 'genq' for GENQ and GENQM fits, else 'qp'.

    		 None
    level float | None

    Confidence level in percent (95 is 95%). As in metafor, a value below 1 is read as the confidence level if it is above 0.5 (0.95) and as the significance level otherwise (0.05). Default: the level of the model.

    		 None
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to each coefficient and bound of the fixed table separately, for example numpy.exp; the bounds are put in order. Default: none.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Second argument passed to transf (transf(value, targs)). Default: none, except for the integral and mode transformations of transf, which get {'tau2': tau2}.

    		 None
    tau2_min float | None

    Lower end of the interval searched for the bounds of tau^2. Default: the smaller of 0 and the estimate (metafor uses the tau2.min of the control of the fitted model instead if it was set; metafopy does not). Replaced by the entry of control or by xlim.

    		 None
    tau2_max float | None

    Upper end of the interval searched for the bounds. Default: the largest of 100, ten times the estimate and ten times the lower end.

    		 None
    tol float

    Convergence tolerance of the root finding (default eps^0.25). Not used for type='genq', which uses the defaults of R's uniroot as metafor does.

    		 DEFAULT_TOL
    maxiter int

    Maximum number of iterations of the root finding (not used for type='genq').

    		 1000
    verbose bool | int

    Print the steps of the root finding for the types 'qp', 'genq' and 'pl' on stdout, as metafor does; with digits decimals.

    		 False
    digits int | None

    Number of decimals used for verbose output and the printout of the result. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

    		 None
    control Mapping[str, Any] | None

    metafor's list of root-finding settings (tau2_min, tau2_max, tol and maxiter, written with . or _). Its entries replace the keyword arguments of the same name. Names must be given in full (metafor accepts partial names); entries that only other functions of metafor read, including verbose, are ignored here, and any other entry raises InputError.

    		 None
    xlim float | Sequence[float] | None

    Interval (tau2_min, tau2_max) searched for the bounds (metafor's ... argument); a single value is the upper limit and the lower one is 0. Wins over control.

    		 None
    extint bool

    Let the search for a profile-likelihood bound (type='pl') widen the interval (R's extendInt; metafor's ... argument).

    		 False
    parm Any

    Ignored, with a warning, as in metafor.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    ConfintResult

    A ConfintResult with the fixed table (coefficients) and/or the random table (tau^2, tau, I^2(%),
    ConfintResult

    H^2), each with the columns estimate, ci.lb and ci.ub. A bound the search cannot find is NaN, with a warning.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    an argument is invalid (unknown type or control entry, neither fixed nor random, xlim of the wrong length, a search interval that does not contain the estimate for type='pl', type='genq' for a fit that is not GENQ or GENQM, type='ht' with moderators or k <= 2, type='qp' with non-positive sampling variances), k = 1, or the model has no estimated random-effects component (equal-effects methods, or a fixed tau^2).

    Give Wald-type intervals for the coefficients (t distribution with the degrees of freedom of each coefficient unless the test is 'z'). Without a component argument only these are returned; with one, the interval of the component is returned too.

    		 False

    0-based position of the sigma2 component to compute the interval for. Only one of sigma2, tau2, rho, gamma2 and phi may be given.

    phi int | None

    Lower end of the interval searched for the bounds of a component. Default: 0 for sigma2, tau2 and gamma2; for rho and phi -1, except min(0, estimate) for the structures 'AR', 'HAR' and 'CAR' and 0 for the spatial structures. Replaced by control or xlim.

    vc_max float | None

    Upper end of the interval searched for the bounds. Default: for sigma2, tau2 and gamma2 the larger of 10 and 100 times the estimate (10 if the estimate is practically 0); for rho and phi 1, except max(10, 10 * estimate) for the structures 'SPEXP', 'SPGAU', 'SPLIN', 'SPRAT' and 'SPSPH' and max(2, 2 * estimate) for 'PHYPL' and 'PHYPD'.

    parm Any

    confint_rma_ls(
    model: RMALSResult,
    *,
    fixed: bool = False,
    alpha: int | None = None,

    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    control: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    tol: float = DEFAULT_TOL,
    maxiter: int = 1000,
    eptries: int = 10,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,

    parm: Any = None,
    digits: int | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> ConfintResult | ConfintList

    Confidence intervals for the scale (or location) coefficients of a location-scale model (metafor's confint.rma.ls).

    Intervals for the scale coefficients are profile-likelihood intervals. The intervals for the location coefficients (fixed=True) are of Wald type.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model RMALSResult

    Location-scale model fitted by rma_uni with scale.

    		 required
    fixed bool

    Give Wald-type intervals for the location coefficients (t distribution if the test is 't', 'knha' or 'adhoc', else normal). Without alpha only these are returned; with alpha, the interval of the scale coefficient is returned too.

    		 False
    alpha int | None

    0-based position of the scale coefficient to compute the profile-likelihood interval for. Default: all estimated scale coefficients (unless fixed=True).

    		 None
    level float | None

    Confidence level in percent (95 is 95%). As in metafor, a value below 1 is read as the confidence level if it is above 0.5 (0.95) and as the significance level otherwise (0.05). Default: the level of the model.

    		 None
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to each location coefficient and bound (with fixed=True) separately; the bounds are put in order. Default: none.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Second argument passed to transf (transf(value, targs)). Default: none (the integral and mode transformations get no default tau2).

    		 None
    control Mapping[str, Any] | None

    Settings of the root finding: vc_min and vc_max (also written vc.min, vc.max; the interval searched for the bounds), tol, maxiter, eptries and verbose (the entry verbose has no effect, see verbose). Its entries replace the keyword arguments of the same name. Names must be given in full; entries that only other functions of metafor read are ignored and any other entry raises InputError. The default interval searched for the bounds of a coefficient is its estimate plus and minus the smaller of ten times its absolute value and ten times the normal critical value times its standard error (the former only if the standard error is NaN), limited by alpha_min and alpha_max of the control of the fitted model.

    		 None
    tol float

    Convergence tolerance of the root finding (default eps^0.25).

    		 DEFAULT_TOL
    maxiter int

    Maximum number of iterations of the root finding.

    		 1000
    eptries int

    Number of attempts to find the bounds: when the model cannot be fitted at an end of the interval searched, that end is moved towards the estimate by 1 / eptries of the distance and tried again.

    		 10
    xlim Sequence[float] | None

    Interval (vc_min, vc_max) searched for the bounds (metafor's ... argument). Wins over control.

    		 None
    extint bool

    Let the search for a bound widen the interval (R's extendInt).

    		 False
    parm Any

    Ignored, with a warning, as in metafor.

    		 None
    digits int | None

    Number of decimals of the printout. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

    		 None
    verbose bool

    Accepted for compatibility with metafor; it has no effect here (no output is produced).

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    ConfintResult | ConfintList

    A ConfintResult with the estimate, ci.lb and ci.ub of the requested coefficient(s); the scale coefficient
    ConfintResult | ConfintList

    is in the random table (rows alpha.1, alpha.2, ...) and the location coefficients in the fixed table. With no alpha and
    ConfintResult | ConfintList

    several estimated scale coefficients, a ConfintList (a list of results); a single result if there is one. A bound the search cannot find
    ConfintResult | ConfintList

    is NaN, with a warning; a bound at the end of the interval searched is shown with a < or > sign.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    an argument is invalid, control has an unknown entry, the model was fitted with optbeta=True, the model has no such (estimated) scale coefficient or no coefficient to give an interval for, or the interval searched does not contain the estimate.

    ConfintResult dataclass ¶

    ConfintResult(
    fixed: DataFrame | None,
    random: DataFrame | None,
    lb_sign: str = '',
    ub_sign: str = '',
    digits: int | None = None,
    tau2_min: float | None = None,
)

    Bases: HtmlRepr

    Confidence intervals as returned by confint: a fixed table for the coefficients and/or a random table for the variance components. to_frame() stacks the tables and summary() gives metafor's printout.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    fixed DataFrame | None

    Table of the coefficients (fixed=True) with the columns estimate, ci.lb and ci.ub, one row per coefficient, or None.
    random DataFrame | None

    Table of the variance components with the same columns, or None. The rows are tau^2, tau, I^2(%) and H^2 for an rma_uni fit; for an rma_mv fit sigma^2 and sigma, tau^2 and tau or gamma^2 and gamma (one pair), or rho or phi (one row), with the position added (.1, .2, ...) if the model has several; for a location-scale fit alpha.1, alpha.2, ... (alpha if there is one).
    lb_sign str

    Prefix printed before the lower bounds of random: '<' if the bound lies below the lower end of the interval searched, '>' if it lies above the upper end, else ''.
    ub_sign str

    Prefix printed before the upper bounds of random, as lb_sign.
    digits int | None

    Number of decimals used when printing (None if not set).
    tau2_min float | None

    Lower end of the interval searched for the bounds of tau^2 (rma_uni fits with random=True, else None).

    ci_null property ¶

    ci_null: bool

    metafor's ci.null: the whole interval of the variance component lies at or below the lower limit of the search (that limit is zero or less).

    to_frame ¶

    to_frame() -> DataFrame

    The fixed and random tables stacked into one data frame (the columns are estimate, ci.lb and ci.ub).

    summary ¶

    summary(
    digits: int | Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
) -> str

    The printout of metafor's print.confint.rma: the table of the coefficients, then that of the variance components.

    Tests and profiles¶

    anova ¶

    anova(model: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any

    Wald tests of coefficients or likelihood-ratio tests of nested models for fitted models (metafor's anova).

    This is a single-dispatch function: the implementation is chosen by the class of model. See anova_rma_uni, anova_rma_mv and anova_rma_ls.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model Any

    The fitted model. Its class selects the implementation.

    		 required
    *args Any

    Positional arguments passed on to the implementation (a second model first).

    		 ()
    **kwargs Any

    Keyword arguments passed on to the implementation.

    		 {}

    Returns:

    Type Description
    Any

    A WaldResult (Wald test), an LRTResult (likelihood-ratio test of two rma_uni models), a
    Any

    MVLRTResult (likelihood-ratio test of two rma_mv or location-scale models), an LSWaldResult (Wald test for a location-scale
    Any

    model), or a list of Wald results for a list of tests.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ArgumentError

    there is no implementation for the class of model. An argument the implementation does not have is a TypeError from Python, as for any function.

    anova_rma_uni ¶

    anova_rma_uni(
    model: RMAResult,
    model2: RMAResult | None = None,
    *,
    object2: RMAResult | None = None,
    btt: int | Sequence[int] | str | None = None,
    X: ArrayLike | PairmatSpec | None = None,
    rhs: ArrayLike | float | None = None,
    adjust: bool | str | None = None,
    refit: bool = False,
    L: ArrayLike | None = None,
    fixed: bool = False,
    test: str | None = None,
    df: int | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
    abbrev: bool = False,
    digits: int | Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    att: Any = None,
    Z: Any = None,
) -> WaldResult | LRTResult | ListAnovaResult

    Test coefficients of one rma_uni model, or compare two nested models (metafor's anova.rma).

    anova(res, btt=...) tests a subset of coefficients, anova(res, X=L) tests linear combinations L beta = rhs and anova(full, reduced) gives a likelihood-ratio test.

    For a model made robust with club_sandwich=True the omnibus test is the cluster-robust Wald test with the small-sample approximation chosen by wald_test of robust (HTZ by default: an F test with df1 and df2 from clubSandwich::Wald_test), and the tests of linear combinations use the degrees of freedom of coef_test. As in R, rhs cannot be used with X for such a model (a warning is given and zero is used).

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/anova.rma.r

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model RMAResult

    Model fitted by rma_uni.

    		 required
    model2 RMAResult | None

    A second, nested model fitted to the same data, of the same class, for a likelihood-ratio test. The model with more parameters is the full model; when df is given, model is the full model. Default: none, which gives a Wald test of the coefficients of model.

    		 None
    object2 RMAResult | None

    R's name for model2; giving both with different values raises InputError.

    		 None
    btt int | Sequence[int] | str | None

    Coefficients to test jointly: 0-based indices (sorted and without duplicates; an index outside the model raises InputError), a string matched with re.search against the coefficient names (see fixed; metafor uses grep), or a list of several strings or index lists for one test each (a list result, named by the specifications). Default: the coefficients tested by the omnibus test of the model, all but the intercept if there is one.

    		 None
    X ArrayLike | PairmatSpec | None

    Linear combinations of the coefficients to test: a 1-d array (one combination) or a 2-d array with one row per combination, with all p columns or without the intercept column (a column of ones is then added). Each row is tested against rhs; the result holds one test per row and, if X has full row rank, the omnibus test of all of them (QM is otherwise NaN). Also accepted: a pairmat specification. Default: none.

    		 None
    rhs ArrayLike | float | None

    Right-hand side of the hypotheses: a number or one value per combination (or per tested coefficient with btt; a different length raises InputError). Default: 0.

    		 None
    adjust bool | str | None

    Adjust the p-values for multiple testing, as R's p.adjust: True for 'bonferroni', False for 'none', or one of 'holm', 'hochberg', 'hommel', 'bonferroni', 'BH', 'BY', 'fdr' and 'none' (a unique prefix is accepted). It applies to the p-values of the individual tests of the linear combinations, and to the omnibus p-value of a test of moderators (across the elements for a list btt). Default: no adjustment.

    		 None
    refit bool

    For a likelihood-ratio test of REML models whose fixed effects differ, refit them with ML first (otherwise a warning is given).

    		 False
    L ArrayLike | None

    Old spelling of X; if both are given, L is used.

    		 None
    fixed bool

    Match a string btt as a literal substring of the coefficient names instead of as a regular expression.

    		 False
    test str | None

    With model2: 'LRT' (default) for the likelihood-ratio test, or 'Wald' to test the coefficients that only the full model has, with the Wald test of that model (the models must use the same method). A unique prefix is accepted; anything else raises ArgumentError.

    		 None
    df int | None

    With model2: the degrees of freedom of the likelihood-ratio test, instead of the difference in the number of parameters (it is also added to the number of parameters of the full model).

    		 None
    verbose bool

    Add the reason to the error of a cluster-robust test that fails.

    		 False
    abbrev bool

    Remove factor( and ) from the text of the hypotheses of a test of linear combinations (not described on metafor's reference page, but accepted by its source).

    		 False
    digits int | Mapping[str, int] | None

    Number of decimals of the printout of the result (also used for the hypotheses of a test of linear combinations), or a mapping as for predict. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

    		 None
    att Any

    For location-scale models only; giving it here raises InputError.

    		 None
    Z Any

    For location-scale models only; giving it here raises InputError.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    WaldResult | LRTResult | ListAnovaResult

    For a Wald test, a WaldResult with the omnibus statistic QM, its degrees of freedom QMdf and p-value QMp and,
    WaldResult | LRTResult | ListAnovaResult

    for linear combinations, the estimates Xb, se, zval, pval and the hypotheses hyp. For two models, an
    WaldResult | LRTResult | ListAnovaResult

    LRTResult (or, with test='Wald', a WaldResult). For a list btt, a ListAnovaResult (a list of Wald results).

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    an argument or the data is invalid (for example att or Z is given, X has the wrong number of columns, btt selects nothing, adjust is unknown, the models differ in class or data or in the number of parameters, or a cluster-robust test cannot be computed).
    ArgumentError

    test is neither 'LRT' nor 'Wald'.
    InternalError

    an internal invariant does not hold.
    Metafor reference

    hettest ¶

    hettest(
    x: RMAResult
    | RMAMVResult
    | FixedBinaryResult
    | RMALSResult
    | SelmodelResult
    | GLMMResult
    | ArrayLike
    | str,
    vi: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    *,
    sei: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    subset: ArrayLike | None = None,
    data: DataFrame | None = None,
    method: str | None = None,
    test: str | Sequence[str] = 'score',
    boot: bool | int | Sequence[bool] = True,
    progbar: bool = False,
    digits: int | None = None,
    control: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
    mom: bool = False,
    model: RMAResult | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> HettestResult

    Test for heteroscedastic heterogeneity in a random-effects model (metafor's hettest).

    The standard random-effects model assumes that the heterogeneity of the true effects is homoscedastic; this tests that assumption against study-specific tau^2_i values, with a likelihood-ratio, Wald-type or score test, or with goodness-of-fit tests of the Pearson residuals. P-values come from a parametric bootstrap, the first sample being the data. Without seed the bootstrap uses the generator of set_seed.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x RMAResult | RMAMVResult | FixedBinaryResult | RMALSResult | SelmodelResult | GLMMResult | ArrayLike | str

    Effect size estimates (an array, or a column name of data), or a random-effects model without moderators (rma_uni), normally fitted by ML or REML. For a model fitted with another method a warning is given and the test is based on method. Models with moderators and other classes of model raise an error.

    		 required
    vi ArrayLike | str | None

    Sampling variances (array or column name). Ignored (with a warning) if x is a model.

    		 None
    sei ArrayLike | str | None

    Standard errors, instead of vi (array or column name). Ignored (with a warning) if x is a model.

    		 None
    subset ArrayLike | None

    Which studies to use: a boolean array or 0-based indices. Ignored (with a warning) if x is a model.

    		 None
    data DataFrame | None

    Data frame holding the variables named in x, vi and sei.

    		 None
    method str | None

    'REML' (default) or 'ML' (case-sensitive; anything else raises InputError). Ignored (with a warning) if x is a model fitted by ML or REML, whose own method is used.

    		 None
    test str | Sequence[str]

    One test or a sequence of tests (case insensitive): 'score' (default), 'lrt' (likelihood ratio), 'wald', or the goodness-of-fit tests of the Pearson residuals 'ksn', 'ksx2', 'adn' and 'adx2' (Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Anderson-Darling tests of normality and of the chi-square distribution of the squared residuals). The goodness-of-fit tests always bootstrap.

    		 'score'
    boot bool | int | Sequence[bool]

    True bootstraps with 1000 samples, a number sets the number of samples (and bootstraps every test), False uses the chi-square approximation with k - 1 degrees of freedom. May be a sequence of bools, one per test (or one for all). The goodness-of-fit tests always bootstrap.

    		 True
    progbar bool

    Print a progress bar to stderr during the bootstrap. Unlike metafor, off by default.

    		 False
    digits int | None

    Number of decimals of the printout. Default: the digits option, else that of the model x (4 for a vector).

    		 None
    control Mapping[str, Any] | None

    Mapping of control values (names written with . or _): tau2i_init (starting values of the tau^2_i: one value or one per study, not negative; default: the tau^2 of the null model, but at least 0.01), threshold (convergence threshold, 1e-8) and maxiter (1000). Not used if x is a model, as in metafor. Names must be given in full (metafor accepts partial names).

    		 None
    seed int | None

    Seed for the bootstrap: it re-seeds the generator of set_seed, as set.seed(seed) does in R, before the samples are drawn. Default: continue with that generator.

    		 None
    mom bool

    Estimate the tau^2_i by the method of moments (max(0, e_i^2 / (1 - h_i) - v_i)).

    		 False
    model RMAResult | None

    For a vector x: an intercept-only model already fitted to the same data, used as the null model instead of fitting it again (metafor's undocumented argument).

    		 None
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    As R's na.action: studies with missing values in a vector x are omitted with a warning ('omit', 'exclude' and 'pass' act alike), except for 'fail', which raises. No effect for a fitted model.

    		 'omit'
    verbose bool

    Read by metafor but without effect there as well; no effect here.

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    HettestResult

    A HettestResult with one entry per requested test in statistic, df, pval, test and boot, plus
    HettestResult

    tau2i, se_tau2i (Wald-type test) and the bootstrapped statistics statistic_boot.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    an argument or the data is invalid (unknown test, method or control entry, wrong length of boot or tau2i_init, k <= 1, a model with moderators), the null model or the tau^2_i could not be estimated, or studies are missing and na_action='fail'.
    NotSupportedError

    x is a model of a class the test is not available for.
    Metafor reference

    hettest

    statistic: FloatArray,

    test: tuple[str, ...],
    boot: tuple[bool, ...],
    iter: int,
    digits: int,
    tau2i: FloatArray | None,
    se_tau2i: FloatArray | None = None,
    statistic_boot: FloatArray | None = None,
)

    Result of hettest. summary() gives the printout of metafor's print.hettest.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    statistic FloatArray

    Test statistic, one per requested test.
    df FloatArray

    Degrees of freedom, one per test (k - 1 for the likelihood-ratio, Wald-type and score tests, NaN for goodness-of-fit tests).
    pval FloatArray

    p-value, one per test (bootstrap p-value for the tests that used the bootstrap, else from the chi-square distribution).
    method str

    Estimation method the tests are based on, 'ML' or 'REML'.
    test tuple[str, ...]

    The requested tests, in lower case.
    boot tuple[bool, ...]

    Whether each test used the bootstrap (always True for the goodness-of-fit tests).
    iter int

    Number of bootstrap samples (1000 unless boot was a number).
    digits int

    Number of decimals of the printout.
    tau2i FloatArray | None

    Estimated study-specific heterogeneity variances of the saturated model, one per study (None if the iterations did not converge and no test needed them).
    se_tau2i FloatArray | None

    Standard errors of tau2i (only with the Wald-type test, else None).
    statistic_boot FloatArray | None

    Bootstrapped statistics, an array with one row per sample and one column per test (None if no test used the bootstrap; NaN for samples that failed, and for the tests that did not use the bootstrap). The first sample is the data itself.

    permutest_rma_uni ¶

    permutest_rma_uni(
    x: RMAResult,
    exact: bool | Literal['i'] = False,
    iter: int = 1000,
    btt: int | Sequence[int] | str | None = None,
    permci: bool | Sequence[int] = False,
    digits: int | None = None,
    control: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    *,
    seed: int | None = None,
    tol: float | None = None,
    fixed: bool = False,
    progbar: bool = False,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> PermutestResult | int | float

    Permutation test for an rma_uni fit (metafor's permutest.rma.uni).

    For a model without moderators the signs of the estimates are permuted, otherwise the rows of the model matrix. The p-value is the proportion of permutations whose statistic is as extreme as the observed one (the first permutation of an approximate test is the data, which avoids p-values of 0). With few studies the smallest possible p-value can exceed 0.05.

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/permutest.rma.uni.r

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x RMAResult

    Model fitted by rma_uni (not a robust result).

    		 required
    exact bool | Literal['i']

    True carries out an exact test (all unique permutations; also used if iter exceeds their number); 'i' returns the number of iterations an exact test needs; False (default) uses iter random permutations.

    		 False
    iter int

    Number of random permutations for an approximate test (at least 2).

    		 1000
    btt int | Sequence[int] | str | None

    Coefficients the omnibus test refers to: 0-based indices or a string searched for (Python re.search) in the coefficient names. Default: that of the model.

    		 None
    permci bool | Sequence[int]

    True, or 0-based coefficient indices, to also find permutation-based confidence interval bounds (slow). A bound that cannot be found is NaN.

    		 False
    digits int | None

    Number of decimals of the printout. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

    		 None
    control Mapping[str, Any] | None

    Mapping with metafor's control values: comptol (tolerance of the comparisons), tol and maxiter (root finding for permci), alternative ('two.sided', 'less' or 'greater'), p2defn ('abs' or 'px2'), stat ('test' or 'coef'), cialt (alternative for the CI bounds) and distfac (factor widening the search interval for the CI bounds).

    		 None
    seed int | None

    Seed of the random permutations. Default: drawn from the R-compatible generator of set_seed, which is left in the state the permutations ended in, as R's global generator is.

    		 None
    tol float | None

    Old spelling of the comptol entry of control.

    		 None
    fixed bool

    Match a string btt literally instead of as a regular expression.

    		 False
    progbar bool

    Print a progress bar to stderr while the permutations are run (default False; metafor's default is TRUE).

    		 False
    verbose bool

    Accepted and ignored (metafor shows the errors of refits that fail during the permutations).

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    PermutestResult | int | float

    A PermutestResult with the coefficient table (beta, se, zval, pval, ci_lb, ci_ub), the omnibus
    PermutestResult | int | float

    test (QM, QMp) and the permutation distributions. With exact='i', the number of iterations an exact test needs.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    iter is below 2; btt or permci names a coefficient that does not exist; a control entry is not accepted; an exact test needs more iterations than the largest float.
    ArgumentError

    control has an unknown entry.
    NotSupportedError

    x is a robust result.
    ValueError

    an exact test needs more iterations than can be allocated (R stops with an error as well).

    Permutation tests for the location and scale coefficients of a location-scale fit (metafor's permutest.rma.ls).

    For the scale part with control={'p2defn': 'px2'}, the current metafor source (permutest.rma.ls.r) refers to x$zval.alpha.[j], which does not exist, so the p-values there are NaN in R; here they are computed from the observed test statistics. An intercept-only scale model skips the scale part with a warning.

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/permutest.rma.ls.r

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x RMALSResult

    Location-scale model fitted by rma_uni with scale.

    		 required
    exact bool | Literal['i']

    True carries out an exact test of each part (all unique permutations); 'i' returns the numbers of iterations an exact test needs for the location and the scale part; False (default) uses iter random permutations.

    		 False
    iter int

    Number of random permutations for an approximate test (at least 2).

    		 1000
    btt int | Sequence[int] | str | None

    Location coefficients the omnibus test refers to: 0-based indices or a string searched for (Python re.search) in the coefficient names. Default: that of the model.

    		 None
    att int | Sequence[int] | str | None

    		 None
    digits int | None

    Number of decimals of the printout. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

    		 None
    control Mapping[str, Any] | None

    Mapping with comptol, alternative, p2defn and stat, as for permutest.

    		 None
    seed int | None

    Seed of the generator for each approximate part. Default: drawn from the generator of set_seed.

    		 None
    tol float | None

    Old spelling of the comptol entry of control.

    		 None
    skip_beta bool

    Skip the permutation test of the location part.

    		 False
    skip_alpha bool

    Skip the permutation test of the scale part.

    		 False
    progbar bool

    Print a progress bar to stderr for each part (default False; metafor's default is TRUE).

    		 False
    permci bool

    Only warns, as permutation-based confidence intervals are not available for location-scale models in metafor either.

    		 False
    fixed bool

    Match a string btt or att literally instead of as a regular expression.

    		 False
    verbose bool

    Accepted and ignored (metafor shows the errors of refits that fail during the permutations).

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    LSPermutestResult | list[float]

    A result (an LSPermutestResult) with the permutation tests of the location part and of the scale part. With exact='i', a list with the
    LSPermutestResult | list[float]

    numbers of iterations an exact test needs.

)

    Bases: HtmlRepr

    Permutation-based p-values (and optionally CI bounds) for the coefficients of a model, as returned by permutest. to_frame() and coef() give the coefficient table and summary() the printout.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    pval FloatArray

    Permutation p-values of the coefficients.
    QMdf tuple[int, int | None]

    Degrees of freedom of the omnibus test, (m, None) for the z test and (m, ddf) for the t test.
    QMp float

    Permutation p-value of the omnibus test.
    beta FloatArray

    Estimates of the coefficients.
    se FloatArray

    Standard errors of the coefficients.
    zval FloatArray

    Test statistics of the coefficients.
    ci_lb FloatArray

    Lower confidence interval bounds (permutation-based with permci, else the usual ones).
    ci_ub FloatArray

    Upper confidence interval bounds.
    QM float

    Test statistic of the omnibus test.
    k int

    Number of studies.
    p int

    Number of coefficients.
    btt tuple[int, ...]

    Coefficients (0-based) the omnibus test refers to.
    m int

    Number of coefficients in the omnibus test.
    test str

    Test used by the model: 'z', 't', 'knha' or 'adhoc'.
    ddf int | None

    Residual degrees of freedom of the t test, or None for the z test.
    int_only bool

    Whether the model has only an intercept.
    int_incl bool

    Whether the model has an intercept.
    coef_names tuple[str, ...]

    Names of the coefficients.
    exact_iter int | float

    Number of iterations an exact test needs (inf if it exceeds the largest float).
    permci bool

    Whether permutation-based CI bounds were computed (False if permci was requested but the number of permutations is too low for the confidence level).
    alternative str

    Alternative hypothesis of the test (the alternative control entry; with permutation-based CI bounds, the one of the last bound search, as in metafor).
    p2defn str

    Definition of the two-sided p-value.
    stat str

    Statistic used for the coefficients.
    QM_perm FloatArray

    Omnibus statistics of every permutation (for the approximate test the first one is the observed one, as in metafor).
    zval_perm DataFrame

    Test statistics of every permutation, one column per coefficient.
    beta_perm DataFrame

    Estimates of every permutation, one column per coefficient.
    digits int

    Number of decimals of the printout.

    dfs property ¶

    dfs: int | None

    R's dfs: the residual degrees of freedom (ddf) of the test.

    skip_beta property ¶

    skip_beta: bool

    R's skip.beta: the plain model never skips the coefficients.

    Profile likelihood of a variance component of a fitted model (metafor's profile).

    This is a single-dispatch function: the implementation is chosen by the class of fitted. See profile_rma_uni, profile_rma_ls, profile_rma_mv; selection models (selmodel) are also supported.

    fitted Any

    a MVProfileResult for an rma_mv fit and a
    ProfileResult

    profile_rma_uni(
    fitted: RMAResult,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    ylim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    steps: int | ArrayLike = 20,
    lltol: float = 0.001,
    plot: bool = False,
    *,
    sqrt: bool = False,
    exp: bool = False,
    ax: Any = None,
    progbar: bool = False,
    parallel: Literal['no', 'snow', 'multicore'] = 'no',
    ncpus: int = 1,
    cl: Executor | None = None,
    pred: bool = False,
    blup: bool = False,
    newmods: ArrayLike
    | Mapping[str, float]
    | Series
    | DataFrame
    | None = None,
    LB: bool = False,
    **plot_args: Any,
) -> ProfileResult

    Profile the likelihood of an rma_uni fit over tau^2 (metafor's profile.rma.uni).

    The model is refitted with tau^2 fixed at each value of a grid and the log-likelihood (and the coefficients) recorded. xlim defaults to the range spanned by the Q-profile CI for tau^2 and the estimate (the upper end at least 0.1). Models with equal or fixed effects cannot be profiled.

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/profile.rma.uni.r

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    fitted RMAResult

    Random- or mixed-effects model fitted by rma_uni (not an equal- or fixed-effects model).

    		 required
    xlim Sequence[float] | None

    Range (lower, upper) of tau^2 values (tau values with sqrt=True). Default: the range spanned by the Q-profile CI for tau^2 and the estimate.

    		 None
    ylim Sequence[float] | None

    Range (lower, upper) of the profile log-likelihood stored in the result (and drawn by the plot). Default: the range of the profile and the maximum.

    		 None
    steps int | ArrayLike

    Number of equally spaced values in xlim to profile over (a single number, at least 2), or a sequence of two or more values to profile at (then xlim defaults to their range). Missing values are not allowed.

    		 20
    lltol float

    Tolerance when checking whether a profiled log-likelihood exceeds that of the fitted model (a warning is given if it does).

    		 0.001
    plot bool

    Draw the profile with plot_profile (default False; metafor's default is TRUE).

    		 False
    sqrt bool

    Profile over tau instead of tau^2 (the grid and xlim are then on the tau scale).

    		 False
    exp bool

    Report the likelihood instead of the log-likelihood (exponentiate it; ylim is then not widened by 0.1).

    		 False
    ax Any

    Matplotlib axes to draw on (with plot=True). Default: a new figure.

    		 None
    progbar bool

    Print a progress bar to stderr while the models of the grid are fitted (default False; metafor's default is TRUE).

    		 False
    parallel Literal['no', 'snow', 'multicore']

    Parallel fitting of the grid: 'no' (default), 'snow' or 'multicore'; both use a process pool ('multicore' forks the workers where the platform allows). As in metafor, 'no' with ncpus > 1 (or with cl) is 'snow', and 'snow' or 'multicore' with ncpus < 2 and no cl runs serially. The result equals that of the serial run. Any other value raises an InputError.

    		 'no'
    ncpus int

    Number of worker processes (at least 1).

    		 1
    cl Executor | None

    Executor to run the fits on instead of creating a process pool of ncpus workers.

    		 None
    pred bool

    Also store the predicted values of each refit (for newmods, or the fitted values without it, as predict); metafor's undocumented argument.

    		 False
    blup bool

    Also store the BLUPs (blup) of each refit; metafor's undocumented argument.

    		 False
    newmods ArrayLike | Mapping[str, float] | Series | DataFrame | None

    Moderator values for the predictions stored with pred=True, as for predict.

    		 None
    LB bool

    Accepted as in metafor, where it chooses parLapplyLB; it changes no result.

    		 False
    **plot_args Any

    Further keyword arguments passed on to plot_profile (pch, cline, refline, xlab, ylab, main, log, cex, lwd), as metafor's ... is to plot.profile.rma; they are not used (and not checked) with plot=False.

    		 {}

    Returns:

    Type Description
    ProfileResult

    The profile, a ProfileResult with the grid tau2, the log-likelihoods ll, the coefficients and their CI bounds at
    ProfileResult

    each grid value, and the estimate vc and maximum log-likelihood maxll of the model.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    the model uses an equal- or fixed-effects method; steps has missing values or is a single number below 2; xlim or ylim does not have length 2; xlim cannot be set automatically; parallel is not one of the accepted values or ncpus is below 1; with pred=True no predictions can be computed.

As in metafor, 'no' with ncpus > 1 (or with cl) is 'snow', and 'snow' or 'multicore' with ncpus < 2 and no cl runs serially. The result equals that of the serial run. Any other value raises an InputError.

) -> MVProfileResult | list[MVProfileResult]

    Profile the likelihood of an rma_mv fit over one variance or correlation component (metafor's profile.rma.mv).

    Without any of sigma2, tau2, rho, gamma2 and phi every estimated component is profiled and a list is returned (a single result if there is just one; several are a ProfileList). xlim defaults to metafor's range around the estimate: for a variance a quarter to four times the estimate (half to twice for tau2 and gamma2 with a spatial structure), at least up to 0.1; for a correlation the estimate +- 0.5 within (-1, 1) (from 0 for 'CAR', half to twice the estimate for the spatial structures).

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/profile.rma.mv.r

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    fitted RMAMVResult

    Model fitted by rma_mv.

    		 required
    sigma2 int | None

    0-based position of the sigma2 component to profile (metafor counts from 1). Only one of sigma2, tau2, rho, gamma2 and phi may be given.

    		 None
    tau2 int | None

    0-based position of the tau2 component to profile.

    		 None
    rho int | None

    0-based position of the rho component to profile.

    		 None
    gamma2 int | None

    0-based position of the gamma2 component to profile.

    		 None
    phi int | None

    0-based position of the phi component to profile.

    		 None
    xlim Sequence[float] | None

    Range (lower, upper) of the profiled values of the component, within the parameter space (a variance at least 0, a correlation within -1 and 1, at least 0 for 'CAR' and the spatial structures). Default: metafor's range around the estimate.

    		 None
    ylim Sequence[float] | None

    Range (lower, upper) of the profile log-likelihood stored in the result (and drawn by the plot). Default: the range of the profile and the maximum.

    		 None
    steps int | ArrayLike

    Number of equally spaced values in xlim to profile over (a single number, at least 2), or a sequence of two or more values to profile at (then xlim defaults to their range). Missing values are not allowed.

    		 20
    lltol float

    Tolerance when checking whether a profiled log-likelihood exceeds that of the fitted model (a warning is given if it does).

    		 0.001
    progbar bool

    Print a progress bar to stderr while the models of the grid are fitted (default False; metafor's default is TRUE).

    		 False
    parallel Literal['no', 'snow', 'multicore']

    Parallel fitting of the grid: 'no' (default), 'snow' or 'multicore'; both use a process pool ('multicore' forks the workers where the platform allows). As in metafor, 'no' with ncpus > 1 (or with cl) is 'snow', and 'snow' or 'multicore' with ncpus < 2 and no cl runs serially. The result equals that of the serial run. Any other value raises an InputError.

    		 'no'
    ncpus int

    Number of worker processes (at least 1).

    		 1
    cl Executor | None

    Executor to run the fits on instead of creating a process pool of ncpus workers.

    		 None
    plot bool

    Draw the profile with plot_profile (default False; metafor's default is TRUE).

    		 False
    exp bool

    Report the likelihood instead of the log-likelihood (exponentiate it; ylim is then not widened by 0.1).

    		 False
    ax Any

    LB bool

    **plot_args Any

    Further keyword arguments passed on to plot_profile (pch, cline, refline, xlab, ylab, main, log, cex, lwd), as metafor's ... is to plot.profile.rma; they are not used (and not checked) with plot=False.

    		 {}

    MVProfileResult | list[MVProfileResult]

    (Generalized) variance inflation factors for the coefficients of an rma_uni meta-regression (metafor's vif.rma).

    A VIF of a coefficient (or a GVIF of a set of coefficients) shows how much the variance of its estimate is inflated by correlation with the other moderators; the SIF is the corresponding inflation of the standard error.

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/vif.rma.r

    Sets of location coefficients to compute a (generalized) VIF for, 0-based: an int, a string searched for (Python re.search) in the coefficient names, or a list of ints gives one set (one GVIF); a list with lists or strings among its elements gives one set per element (btt=[1, [2, 3], 4], like metafor's btt=list(2, 3:4, 5)). Default: each coefficient except the intercept gets its own VIF.

    		 None
    att Any

    Must be None: metafor uses it for location-scale models only and so does vif_rma_ls; any other value raises an InputError.

    		 None

    		 False
    reestimate bool

    		 False
    sim bool | int

    Simulate the distribution of each (G)VIF under independence: True for 1000 iterations or a number of iterations (at least 2). The model is refitted with independently permuted variables of the data (a model given as a formula with data) or columns of the model matrix; the result then has sim and prop (nothing is simulated if every (G)VIF is 1). Iteration l is seeded with seed + l when seed is given, as in metafor, otherwise from the stream of set_seed.

As in metafor, 'no' with ncpus > 1 (or with cl) is 'snow', and 'snow' or 'multicore' with ncpus < 2 and no cl runs serially. Any other value raises an InputError.

    Cluster-robust inference¶

    robust ¶

    robust(model: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any

    Cluster-robust (sandwich) inference for a fitted model (metafor's robust).

    This is a single-dispatch function: the implementation is chosen by the class of model. See robust_rma_uni and robust_rma_mv.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model Any

    The fitted model. Its class selects the implementation.

    		 required
    *args Any

    Positional arguments passed on to the implementation (cluster first).

    		 ()
    **kwargs Any

    Keyword arguments passed on to the implementation.

    		 {}

    Returns:

    Type Description
    Any

    A copy of the model with cluster-robust standard errors, tests and confidence intervals.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ArgumentError

    there is no implementation for the class of model.
    InputError

    raised by the implementation for an invalid argument.
    TypeError

    cluster is missing, more than one positional argument is given or a keyword argument is not accepted.

    robust_rma_uni ¶

    robust_rma_uni(
    model: RMAResult,
    cluster: Cluster,
    *,
    adjust: bool | str = True,
    club_sandwich: bool | None = None,
    vcov: str | None = None,
    coef_test: str | None = None,
    conf_test: str | None = None,
    wald_test: str | None = None,
    clubSandwich: bool | None = None,
    digits: int | Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> RMAResult

    Cluster-robust inference for an rma_uni fit (metafor's robust.rma.uni).

    The variance-covariance matrix of the coefficients is replaced by a sandwich estimator that is robust to correlated errors within clusters; tests and confidence intervals use it.

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/robust.rma.uni.r

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model RMAResult

    Model fitted by rma_uni (also a model that was made robust before).

    		 required
    cluster Cluster

    The clustering variable: the name of a column of the data given to the model, or a vector with one value per row of the original data (before subsetting and removal of missing values; a vector with one value per study used in the fit is also accepted). It must not contain missing values.

    		 required
    adjust bool | str

    Small-sample adjustment of the cluster-robust variance-covariance matrix: True (default; CR1, multiplies by n/(n-p), with n clusters and p coefficients), False (CR0), 'Stata1' (or 'Stata') or 'Stata2'. Not used with club_sandwich.

    		 True
    club_sandwich bool | None

    Use the clubSandwich approach (bias-reduced linearization, Satterthwaite degrees of freedom) for the cluster-robust tests and intervals instead of the plain sandwich estimator. Default: False.

    		 None
    vcov str | None

    With club_sandwich (ignored otherwise; this and the next three take exactly the values listed): the variance estimator, 'CR0', 'CR1', 'CR1p', 'CR1S', 'CR2' or 'CR3'. Default: 'CR2'.

    		 None
    coef_test str | None

    With club_sandwich: the test of the coefficients, 'z', 'naive-t', 'naive-tp', 'Satterthwaite' or 'saddlepoint'. The saddlepoint test gives p-values only; the confidence intervals then use conf_test or Satterthwaite. Default: Satterthwaite.

    		 None
    conf_test str | None

    With club_sandwich: the method for the confidence intervals, as coef_test without 'saddlepoint'. Default: that of coef_test.

    		 None
    wald_test str | None

    With club_sandwich: the omnibus test, 'chi-sq', 'Naive-F', 'Naive-Fp', 'HTA', 'HTB', 'HTZ', 'EDF' or 'EDT'. Default: 'HTZ'.

    		 None
    clubSandwich bool | None

    R's spelling of club_sandwich. Giving both with different values is an error.

    		 None
    digits int | Mapping[str, int] | None

    Number of decimals of the printout of the result. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

    		 None
    verbose bool

    Accepted and ignored (metafor shows the errors of a failing clubSandwich computation).

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    RMAResult

    The model with the cluster-robust variance-covariance matrix, standard errors, tests and confidence intervals, an RMAResult
    RMAResult

    of the same form as the input (its robust attribute is set; without club_sandwich the tests are t tests with n - p degrees of
    RMAResult

    freedom).

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    cluster cannot be found, has the wrong length or has missing values; adjust, vcov, coef_test, conf_test or wald_test is not an accepted value (including conf_test='saddlepoint'); club_sandwich and clubSandwich differ; without club_sandwich the number of clusters is not larger than the number of coefficients.
    Metafor reference

    robust
