    Use the clubSandwich approach (bias-reduced linearization, Satterthwaite degrees of freedom) for the cluster-robust tests and intervals instead of the plain sandwich estimator. Default: False.

    		 None
    vcov str | None

    With club_sandwich (ignored otherwise; this and the next three take exactly the values listed): the variance estimator, 'CR0', 'CR1', 'CR1p', 'CR1S', 'CR2' or 'CR3'. Default: 'CR2'.

    		 None
    coef_test str | None

    With club_sandwich: the test of the coefficients, 'z', 'naive-t', 'naive-tp', 'Satterthwaite' or 'saddlepoint'. The saddlepoint test gives p-values only; the confidence intervals then use conf_test or Satterthwaite. Default: Satterthwaite.

    		 None
    conf_test str | None

    With club_sandwich: the method for the confidence intervals, as coef_test without 'saddlepoint'. Default: that of coef_test.

    		 None
    wald_test str | None

    With club_sandwich: the omnibus test, 'chi-sq', 'Naive-F', 'Naive-Fp', 'HTA', 'HTB', 'HTZ', 'EDF' or 'EDT'. Default: 'HTZ'.

    		 None
    clubSandwich bool | None

    R's spelling of club_sandwich. Giving both with different values is an error.

    		 None
    digits int | Mapping[str, int] | None

    Number of decimals of the printout of the result. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

    		 None
    verbose bool

    Accepted and ignored (metafor shows the errors of a failing clubSandwich computation).

    		 False

    The model with the cluster-robust variance-covariance matrix, standard errors, tests and confidence intervals, an
    RMAMVResult

    as for robust_rma_uni; with club_sandwich also: the model has fixed correlation matrices (R) or its random effects are not nested within the clusters.

    Variance-covariance matrices and coefficient tables¶

    vcov ¶

    vcov(
    object: Any,
    type: Literal[
        'fixed',
        'beta',
        'alpha',
        'delta',
        'obs',
        'marginal',
        'fitted',
        'resid',
    ] = 'fixed',
    *,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> DataFrame | dict[str, DataFrame]

    Variance-covariance matrices of a fitted model (metafor's vcov).

    Which matrix is returned depends on type; for 'obs', 'fitted' and 'resid' the frame has one row and column per study of the subset. A deltamethod or matreg result gives its own variance-covariance matrix (vcov.deltamethod, vcov.matreg).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    object Any

    The fitted model (or a deltamethod or matreg result).

    		 required
    type Literal['fixed', 'beta', 'alpha', 'delta', 'obs', 'marginal', 'fitted', 'resid']

    Which matrix: 'fixed' (default; of the coefficients), 'beta' (of the location coefficients), 'alpha' (of the scale coefficients of a location-scale model), 'delta' (of the selection parameters of a selection model), 'obs' (or 'marginal'; of the observed effects), 'fitted' (of the fitted values) or 'resid' (of the residuals). A unique prefix is enough ('f' is ambiguous). Not every type is available for every model.

    		 'fixed'
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    For 'obs', 'fitted' and 'resid': 'omit' (default) keeps the studies used in fitting, 'exclude' and 'pass' all of them (NaN for those not used) and 'fail' raises if any study was left out ('fitted' gives the whole matrix, as in R, and 'resid' always raises, as R fails there too).

    		 'omit'

    Returns:

    Type Description
    DataFrame | dict[str, DataFrame]

    The variance-covariance matrix as a data frame labelled with the coefficient names or study labels; a dict of such frames for a model with several
    DataFrame | dict[str, DataFrame]

    parts and no specific type where that applies.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ArgumentError

    object is not a fitted model, or type='resid' for a fit without hatvalues() (rma_mh, rma_peto, rma_glmm).
    InputError

    type (or an ambiguous prefix of it) or na_action is not valid, 'alpha' for a model without scale part, 'delta' for a model that is not a selection model, studies are missing and na_action='fail' for 'obs', or type='resid' with na_action='fail'.
    NotSupportedError

    'obs' for rma_mh, rma_peto and rma_glmm; 'resid' for robust and selection-model fits.

    rstandard_rma_uni ¶

    rstandard_rma_uni(
    model: RMAResult,
    digits: int | None = None,
    type: Literal['marginal', 'conditional'] = 'marginal',
    *,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> ResidualResult

    Internally standardised residuals of an rma_uni fit (metafor's rstandard.rma.uni).

    With type='marginal' the residuals y - X b are divided by the square roots of the diagonal of (I - H) M (I - H)', where M holds the marginal variances; with type='conditional' the residuals are those from the BLUPs, divided by their conditional standard errors. Conditional residuals are not available for models with non-standard weights.

    R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/rstandard.rma.uni.r

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model RMAResult

    Model fitted by rma_uni (not a robust fit).

    		 required
    digits int | None

    Number of decimals of the printout. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

    		 None
    type Literal['marginal', 'conditional']

    'marginal' (default) for marginal residuals or 'conditional' for conditional residuals (the deviations of the estimates from the BLUPs of the true effects). Exactly one of these two values (R also accepts a unique prefix).

    		 'marginal'
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    What to do with studies left out of the fit because of missing values: 'omit' (default) drops them, 'exclude' and 'pass' keep one row per study with NaN for those left out, 'fail' raises an InputError if there are any. Corresponds to R's na.action option.

    		 'omit'

    Returns:

    Type Description
    ResidualResult

    A ResidualResult with the residuals resid, their standard errors se and the standardised values z, labelled
    ResidualResult

    with the study labels.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    type is not 'marginal' or 'conditional'; type='conditional' for a model with weights given or fitted without weighting; na_action is not valid, or is 'fail' and studies were left out of the fit.
    NotSupportedError

    the model is a robust result.
    Metafor reference

    residuals.rma

    rstudent_rma_mv ¶

    rstudent_rma_mv(
    model: RMAMVResult,
    digits: int = 4,
    progbar: bool = False,
    cluster: str | ArrayLike | None = None,
    reestimate: bool = True,
    parallel: Literal['no', 'snow', 'multicore'] = 'no',
    ncpus: int = 1,
    cl: Executor | None = None,
    LB: bool = False,
    *,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> ResidualResult | ClusterResidualResult

    Externally standardised (deleted) residuals of an rma.mv fit (metafor's rstudent.rma.mv).

    Each observation's residual is computed from the fit without it (without its whole cluster if cluster is given); the variance of the deleted residual is the marginal variance of the deleted observation(s) (computed with the variance components estimated without them) plus the variance of their predicted values from the fit without them. With cluster a ClusterResidualResult is returned, which also holds each cluster's X2 statistic.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model RMAMVResult

    A model fitted by rma_mv; not allowed for a model passed through robust.

    		 required
    digits int

    Number of decimals used when the result is printed (default 4).

    		 4
    progbar bool

    Print a progress bar to stderr while the refits are made (default False).

    		 False
    cluster str | ArrayLike | None

    Clustering variable: a column name of the data the model was fitted to, or a vector with one value per row of that data (before subsetting and removal of rows with missing values, which are applied to it automatically). Whole clusters are then deleted in turn. None (the default) deletes each observation in turn.

    		 None
    reestimate bool

    Re-estimate the variance and correlation components after each deletion (default True). With False they stay at the full-model values, which is faster and only approximate.

    		 True
    parallel Literal['no', 'snow', 'multicore']

    'no' (the default), 'snow' or 'multicore'; run the refits in a process pool (see ncpus).

    		 'no'
    ncpus int

    Number of worker processes (default 1; a value above 1 turns parallel processing on).

    		 1
    cl Executor | None

    An executor to run the refits on, instead of one created for the call.

    		 None
    LB bool

    metafor reads this undocumented extra argument to use load-balanced scheduling with parallel='snow'; accepted here and ignored.

    		 False
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    How observations dropped for missing values are handled: 'omit' (the default; no row for them), 'exclude' or 'pass' (a row of missing values for each) or 'fail' (raise an error).

    A ResidualResult with the deleted residuals resid, their standard errors se and z-values z per

    observation; with cluster, a ClusterResidualResult that adds the X2
    ResidualResult | ClusterResidualResult

    statistic and the number of observations k of each cluster.

    an argument or the data is invalid.

    influence_rma_uni ¶

    influence_rma_uni(
    model: RMAResult,
    digits: int | None = None,
    *,
    btt: int | Sequence[int] | str | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    measure: str = 'all',
    progbar: bool = False,
) -> InfluenceResult | Series | DataFrame | ResidualResult

    Leave-one-out diagnostics for an rma.uni fit (metafor's influence()).

    The model is refitted without each study in turn, which gives the externally standardised residuals, DFFITS, Cook's distances, covariance ratios, DFBETAS, leave-one-out tau^2 and QE, hat values and weights (Viechtbauer & Cheung, 2010, doi:10.1002/jrsm.11). Studies whose refit fails (or loses a coefficient) get NaN.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model RMAResult

    A model fitted by rma_uni; not allowed for a model passed through robust (except with measure='cooks.distance').

    		 required
    digits int | None

    Number of decimals used when the result is printed. None uses the digits option, else the digits of the model.

    		 None
    btt int | Sequence[int] | str | None

    The coefficients Cook's distance and the covariance ratio refer to, as 0-based indices (or a regular expression matched against the coefficient names). None (the default) uses all coefficients.

    		 None
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    How studies dropped for missing values are handled: 'omit' (the default; no row for them), 'exclude' or 'pass' (a row of missing values for each, so the result has one row per supplied study) or 'fail' (raise an error).

    		 'omit'
    measure str

    Metafor's undocumented argument that restricts the result: 'cooks.distance' gives only the Cook's distances (as cooks_distance), 'dfbetas' only the DFBETAS (as dfbetas) and 'rstudent' only the deleted residuals (as rstudent). Any other value (the default is 'all') gives the full result.

    		 'all'
    progbar bool

    Print a progress bar to stderr while the studies are left out in turn (default False); no bar is shown with measure='cooks.distance' or 'rstudent'.

    		 False

    InfluenceResult | Series | DataFrame | ResidualResult

    with '*') and dfbs the DFBETAS. With measure set: a Series of Cook's distances, a DataFrame of DFBETAS, or a
    InfluenceResult | Series | DataFrame | ResidualResult

    ResidualResult.

    an argument or the data is invalid.

    cooks_rma_mv ¶

    cooks_rma_mv(
    model: RMAMVResult,
    progbar: bool = False,
    cluster: str | ArrayLike | None = None,
    reestimate: bool = True,
    parallel: Literal['no', 'snow', 'multicore'] = 'no',

    LB: bool = False,
    *,
    btt: int | Sequence[int] | str | None = None,

        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> Series

    Cook's distance of each observation, or of each cluster (metafor's cooks.distance.rma.mv).

    cluster (a column of the data or a vector for the rows of the original data) deletes whole clusters; the result is then indexed by the sorted cluster ids. btt (0-based) selects the coefficients the distance refers to. With reestimate=False the variance components are not re-estimated in the refits. Cook's distance is the Mahalanobis distance between the predicted values with and without the case (Viechtbauer & Cheung, 2010, doi:10.1002/jrsm.11).

    rstudent: FloatArray,

    m: int,
    digits: int = 4,
    ids: NDArray[intp] | None = None,
    not_na: NDArray[bool_] | None = None,
)

    Bases: HtmlRepr

    Case-deletion diagnostics: one entry per study.

    The inf property is the studies' influence table (columns rstudent, dffits, cook.d, cov.r, tau2.del, QE.del, hat, weight and inf), dfbs the DFBETAS (one column per coefficient) and is_infl marks the studies metafor flags with an asterisk: |DFFITS| > 3 sqrt(p/(k-p)), the lower-tail area of a chi-square distribution with m degrees of freedom cut off by Cook's distance above 50%, hat > 3p/k or any |DFBETAS| > 1.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    rstudent FloatArray

    Externally standardised (deleted) residuals.
    dffits FloatArray

    DFFITS values, the standardised change in the fitted value of each study when it is left out.
    cook_d FloatArray

    Cook's distances.
    cov_r FloatArray

    Covariance ratios.
    tau2_del FloatArray

    Estimates of tau^2 from the fits without each study.
    QE_del FloatArray

    Test statistics for residual heterogeneity from the fits without each study.
    hat FloatArray

    Diagonal elements of the hat matrix.
    weight FloatArray

    Weights of the studies in the model fit, in percent.
    dfbs_array FloatArray

    DFBETAS as an array with one column per coefficient.
    is_infl NDArray[bool_]

    Boolean flags for the influential studies.
    slab tuple[str, ...]

    Study labels, in the order of the rows.
    coef_names tuple[str, ...]

    Names of the model coefficients.
    tau2 float

    Estimate of tau^2 of the full model.
    QE float

    Test statistic for residual heterogeneity of the full model.
    k int

    Number of studies in the full model.
    p int

    Number of coefficients in the full model.
    m int

    Number of coefficients the Cook's distances and covariance ratios refer to (see btt).
    digits int

    Number of decimals used when the result is printed.
    ids NDArray[intp] | None

    0-based positions, among the supplied studies, of the studies in the result, if known.
    not_na NDArray[bool_] | None

    Boolean flags for the studies in the result that were used in the fit (all True with na_action='omit'), if known.

    marks: tuple[str, ...]

    '*' for each influential study, '' otherwise.

    The influence table (metafor's inf): rstudent, dffits, cook.d, cov.r, tau2.del, QE.del, hat, weight and inf ('*' for the influential studies), one row per study; attrs holds slab and digits.

    leave1out_rma_uni ¶

    leave1out_rma_uni(
    x: RMAResult,
    cluster: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    digits: int | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    *,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    progbar: bool = False,
) -> Leave1outResult

    Refit an intercept-only rma.uni model leaving out each study (or each cluster of studies).

    transf is applied to the estimates and CI bounds (the integral and mode transformations default to the model's tau2); the standard errors are then NaN. cluster gives one value per study supplied (or a column name in the data the model was fitted to) and leaves out all studies of one cluster at a time. With na_action='exclude'/'pass' (and no cluster) the output has one row per supplied study.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x RMAResult

    A model without moderators (an equal- or random-effects model) fitted by rma_uni; not allowed for a model passed through robust.

    		 required
    cluster ArrayLike | str | None

    Clustering variable: a column name of the data the model was fitted to, or an array with one value per supplied study. All studies of one cluster are left out at a time and the rows are labelled by the sorted cluster ids. None (the default) leaves out one study at a time. Unlike metafor, missing values in cluster are not rejected.

    		 None
    digits int | None

    Number of decimals used when the result is printed. None uses the digits option, else the digits of the model.

    		 None
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    A function applied to the estimates and confidence interval bounds (for example numpy.exp). The integral and mode transformations of metafopy.transf use the tau2 of the model. The standard errors are then NaN. None (the default) applies no transformation.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Extra argument passed to transf as transf(x, targs). None (the default) calls transf(x).

    		 None
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    How studies dropped for missing values are handled: 'omit' (the default; no row for them), 'exclude' or 'pass' (a row of NaN for each, only without cluster) or 'fail' (which, as in metafor, does not raise an error here and gives the same result as 'omit').

    		 'omit'
    progbar bool

    Print a progress bar to stderr while the refits are made (default False).

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    Leave1outResult

    A Leave1outResult with one row per left-out study or cluster (labelled -<label>) holding the
    Leave1outResult

    re-estimated estimate, se, stat (zval, or tval for t, knha and adhoc tests), pval, ci_lb, ci_ub, Q, Qp, I2
    Leave1outResult

    and H2 (and tau2 for random-effects models). A row is NaN when its refit fails.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    an argument or the data is invalid, the model has moderators or there is a single study.
    NotSupportedError

    the model was passed through robust.
    Metafor reference

    leave1out

    cumul_rma_uni ¶

    cumul_rma_uni(
    x: RMAResult,
    order: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    digits: int | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    collapse: bool = False,
    *,
    decreasing: bool = False,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    progbar: bool = False,
) -> CumulResult

    Fit the intercept-only model to the first i studies for i = 1, ..., k (metafor's cumul.rma.uni).

    A cumulative meta-analysis describes the accumulation of evidence as studies are added, typically in chronological order (Chalmers & Lau, 1993, doi:10.1177/096228029300200204; Lau, Schmid & Chalmers, 1995, doi:10.1016/0895-4356(94)00106-Z). Studies dropped for missing values in the fit are skipped. na_action stands for R's options(na.action=), as in metafor (see https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/cumul.rma.uni.r).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x RMAResult

    A model without moderators (an equal- or random-effects model) fitted by rma_uni; not allowed for a model passed through robust.

    		 required
    order ArrayLike | str | None

    Variable giving the order in which the studies are added, ascending: a column name of the data the model was fitted to, or an array with one value per supplied study. Studies with a missing value are not added. None (the default) uses the original order and ignores collapse.

    		 None
    digits int | None

    Number of decimals used when the result is printed. None uses the digits option, else the digits of the model.

    		 None
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    A function applied to the estimates and confidence interval bounds (for example numpy.exp). The integral and mode transformations of metafopy.transf use the tau2 of the model. The standard errors are then NaN. None (the default) applies no transformation.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Extra argument passed to transf as transf(x, targs). None (the default) calls transf(x).

    		 None
    collapse bool

    Add studies with the same value of order together instead of one at a time (default False).

    		 False
    decreasing bool

    Add the studies in descending order of order (default False). metafor takes this as an undocumented extra argument.

    		 False
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    How studies dropped for missing values are handled: 'omit' (the default; no row for them), 'exclude' or 'pass' (a row of missing values for each) or 'fail' (raise an error).

    		 'omit'
    progbar bool

    Print a progress bar to stderr while the refits are made (default False).

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    CumulResult

    blup_rma_uni ¶

    blup_rma_uni(
    res: RMAResult,
    level: float | None = None,
    digits: int | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    *,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> BlupResult

    BLUPs of the true effects of an rma.uni fit (metafor's blup.rma.uni).

    The prediction for study i shrinks its observed effect towards the model's fitted value (the empirical Bayes estimate of its true effect). Prediction intervals use a normal distribution, or a t-distribution with the model's ddf degrees of freedom (k - p unless dfs was given) when the model was fitted with a t, knha or adhoc test. For equal- and fixed-effects models the BLUPs equal the fitted values. na_action plays the role of R's options(na.action=).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    res RMAResult

    A model fitted by rma_uni.

    		 required
    level float | None

    Level of the prediction intervals in percent (e.g. 95), or a value below 1 read as in metafor (0.95 and 0.05 both give 95 percent). None (the default) uses the level of the model.

    		 None
    digits int | None

    Number of decimals used when the result is printed. None uses the digits option, else the digits of the model.

    		 None
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    A function applied to the predicted values and interval bounds (for example numpy.exp); the standard errors are then NaN. None (the default) applies no transformation.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Extra argument passed to transf as transf(x, targs). None (the default) calls transf(x).

    		 None
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    How studies dropped for missing values are handled: 'omit' (the default; no row for them), 'exclude' or 'pass' (a row of NaN for each, so there is one row per supplied study) or 'fail' (raise an error).

    		 'omit'

    Returns:

    Type Description
    BlupResult

    A BlupResult with the predictions pred, standard errors se and prediction interval bounds pi_lb
    BlupResult

    and pi_ub, one entry per study.

    Raises:

    Type Description

    the model has user-defined weights, na_action is unknown or values are missing with na_action='fail'.

    ranef_rma_mv ¶

    ranef_rma_mv(
    object: RMAMVResult,
    level: float | None = None,
    digits: int | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
    *,
    expand: bool = False,
    vcov: bool = False,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> dict[str, Any] | DataFrame | None

    BLUPs of the random effects of an rma.mv fit: a dict with one data frame (intrcpt, se, pi.lb, pi.ub) per term.

    The ~ 1 | id terms are keyed by their grouping variables (s_names), the ~ inner | outer terms by their formulas ('~inner | outer'), as in metafor. level sets the level of the prediction intervals; transf (with targs) is applied to the predictions and interval bounds and drops the se column. expand=True gives the ~ 1 | id terms one row per observation; vcov=True returns {'pred': ..., 'vcov': ...} with the prediction variance-covariance matrices. For struct='GEN'/'GDIAG' metafor returns (only) the matrix of BLUPs of the first ~ inner | outer term, without standard errors; so does this function. digits and verbose have no effect (digits is not used by metafor either; the progress messages are not reproduced). None for models without random effects.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    object RMAMVResult

    A model fitted by rma_mv.

    		 required
    level float | None

    Level of the prediction intervals in percent (e.g. 95), or a value below 1 read as in metafor (0.95 and 0.05 both give 95 percent). None (the default) uses the level of the model.

    		 None
    digits int | None

    Accepted for compatibility; it has no effect.

    		 None
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    A function applied to the predictions and interval bounds (for example numpy.exp); the se column is then dropped. None (the default) applies no transformation.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Extra argument passed to transf as transf(x, targs). None (the default) calls transf(x).

    		 None
    verbose bool

    Accepted for compatibility; it has no effect.

    		 False
    expand bool

    Give the ~ 1 | id terms one row per observation instead of one per level (default False).

    		 False
    vcov bool

    Also return the variance-covariance matrices of the predictions (default False).

    		 False
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    How observations dropped for missing values are handled: 'omit' (the default; the ~ 1 | id terms have a row for each level that occurs in the observations used), 'exclude' or 'pass' (those terms also have a row of NaN for each level that only occurs in dropped observations) or 'fail' (raise an error if observations were dropped; metafor's ranef.rma.mv has no such check). It has no effect on the ~ inner | outer terms.

    		 'omit'

    gosh(x: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> GoshResult

    GOSH (graphical display of study heterogeneity) analysis of a fitted model.

    This is a single-dispatch function: the implementation is chosen from the class of x. See gosh_rma_uni for rma_uni fits. Fits of rma_mh and rma_peto are also supported (as in metafor), with the same arguments as gosh_rma_uni; the subsets then have one or more tables and the result has the column estimate.

    gosh_rma_uni ¶

    gosh_rma_uni(
    x: RMAResult,
    subsets: int | None = None,
    *,
    seed: int | None = None,
    rng: RRandom | None = None,
    progbar: bool = False,
    parallel: Literal['no', 'snow', 'multicore'] = 'no',
    ncpus: int = 1,
    cl: Executor | None = None,
    LB: bool = False,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> GoshResult

    Fit the model to subsets of the studies (metafor's gosh.rma).

    Olkin, Dahabreh & Trikalinos (2012, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1053) proposed examining the pooled estimate and the heterogeneity statistics of the model fitted to all subsets of the studies; Viechtbauer (2021) generalised this to models with moderators. By default all subsets (with at least p studies, p being the number of coefficients) are used if there are at most 10**6 of them, otherwise 10**6 random subsets are drawn. The subsets are drawn before the fits, so the result equals that of a serial run.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x RMAResult

    A model fitted by rma_uni, with or without moderators; not allowed for a model passed through robust, or for location-scale and selection models.

    		 required
    subsets int | None

    Number of subsets to use. None (the default) uses all subsets if there are at most 10**6, else 10**6 random ones. If it is at least the number of possible subsets, all subsets are used. Must be 2 or more.

    		 None
    seed int | None

    Seed of the R-compatible random number generator used to draw random subsets, so that gosh(res, seed=s) draws the same subset sizes and study indices as R's set.seed(s). None uses the global generator (see set_seed). Only used when random subsets are drawn.

    		 None
    rng RRandom | None

    An R-compatible generator to draw the random subsets from, instead of seed or the global generator.

    		 None
    progbar bool

    Print a progress bar (per block of subsets) to stderr (default False; metafor's default is TRUE).

    		 False
    parallel Literal['no', 'snow', 'multicore']

    'no' (the default), 'snow' or 'multicore'; fit the subsets in a process pool (see ncpus).

    		 'no'
    ncpus int

    Number of worker processes (default 1; a value above 1 turns parallel processing on).

    		 1
    cl Executor | None

    An executor to fit the subsets on, instead of one created for the call.

    		 None
    LB bool

    metafor reads this undocumented extra argument to use load-balanced scheduling with parallel='snow'; accepted here and ignored.

    		 False
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    Stands for R's options(na.action=); metafor only checks that it is one of 'omit' (the default), 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail', and so does this function.

    		 'omit'

    Returns:

    Type Description
    GoshResult

    A GoshResult. Its res data frame has one row per subset (sorted by the number of studies) with the columns
    GoshResult

    k, QE, I2, H2, tau2, tau and the coefficient estimates (estimate for a model without moderators);
    GoshResult

    incl is the matrix of inclusion indicators.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    an argument or the data is invalid.
    NotSupportedError

    the model is of a class that is not supported (see x).
    Metafor reference

    cluster: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    subgroup: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    obs: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    type: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    time1: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    time2: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    grp1: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    grp2: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    w1: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    w2: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    data: DataFrame | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    rho: float
    | ArrayLike
    | DataFrame
    | Sequence[Any]
    | None = None,
    phi: float | None = None,
    rvars: Sequence[str | int] | slice | None = None,
    checkpd: bool = True,
    nearpd: bool = False,
    sparse: bool = False,
    retdat: bool = False,
) -> NDArray[float64] | csr_array | DataFrame

    Variance-covariance matrix of dependent estimates, block diagonal over cluster (metafor's vcalc).

    Rows with the same cluster (and subgroup) may be dependent, rows of different clusters are independent. Within a cluster the correlation of two estimates is built from rho (estimates of the same or of different constructs), from phi and the time points time1/time2 (an autoregressive structure), and from the groups grp1/grp2 with sizes w1/w2 for estimates that are contrasts between two conditions and so share a condition. The matrix can be used as the V argument of rma_mv. With rvars the correlation matrices of the clusters are read from columns of data instead.

    Differences from R: metafor's undocumented nearPD alias of nearpd is not accepted; in rvars mode the matrix of a cluster is placed at that cluster's rows even when the rows of a cluster are not contiguous (R places the blocks in order of first appearance, which misaligns the matrix in that case).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    vi ArrayLike | str | None

    Sampling variances of the estimates, as an array or the name of a column of data. Required. A single value is repeated for as many rows as cluster has.

    		 None
    cluster ArrayLike | str | None

    Clustering variable (for example the study), an array or a column name. Required, without missing values. Rows with the same value may be dependent.

    		 None
    subgroup ArrayLike | str | None

    Variable distinguishing independent subgroups within clusters (no overlap of subjects), an array or a column name. Rows of different subgroups are independent even in the same cluster. None for no subgroups.

    		 None
    obs ArrayLike | str | None

    Variable distinguishing different estimates of the same construct or response variable (for example several scales for depression), an array or a column name. Needs rho.

    		 None
    type ArrayLike | str | None

    Variable distinguishing different types of constructs or response variables, an array or a column name. Needs rho.

    		 None
    time1 ArrayLike | str | None

    Numeric time points at which the estimates were obtained (in the first condition for contrasts), an array or a column name. Needs phi.

    		 None
    time2 ArrayLike | str | None

    Numeric time points in the second condition for contrasts between two conditions, an array or a column name.

    		 None
    grp1 ArrayLike | str | None

    Group of the first condition for estimates that are contrasts between two conditions (for example [2, 3] with grp2=[1, 1] for two treatments versus one control), an array or a column name. Give grp1 alone or with grp2.

    		 None
    grp2 ArrayLike | str | None

    Group of the second condition, an array or a column name.

    		 None
    w1 ArrayLike | str | None

    Size of the group of the first condition (or more generally its inverse-sampling-variance weight), numeric, an array or a column name. Default: equal group sizes, which implies a correlation of 0.5 between contrasts that share a condition.

    		 None
    w2 ArrayLike | str | None

    Size (weight) of the group of the second condition, numeric, an array or a column name.

    		 None
    data DataFrame | Mapping[str, Any] | None

    Data frame (or mapping of columns) holding the variables named above.

    		 None
    rho float | ArrayLike | DataFrame | Sequence[Any] | None

    Correlation of the sampling errors of estimates measured concurrently. A scalar, or a correlation matrix as a data frame whose row and column labels are the unique values of obs (or of type). With both obs and type a pair: the first element (a scalar or matrix) is the within-construct correlation among the obs values, the second the between-construct correlation among the type values.

    		 None
    phi float | None

    Autocorrelation of the sampling errors of two estimates that differ by one unit of time1.

    		 None
    rvars Sequence[str | int] | slice | None

    Columns of data that hold the correlation matrices of the clusters: names or 0-based positions, or a slice of names (slice('r1', 'r4') for R's r1:r4). The first k_i columns hold the lower triangle of the matrix of the i-th cluster (k_i rows); there must be as many columns as the largest cluster has rows. When given, all variable arguments except vi, cluster and subgroup are ignored. Needs data.

    		 None
    checkpd bool

    Warn about clusters whose variance-covariance matrix is not positive definite (default True).

    		 True
    nearpd bool

    Replace such matrices by the nearest correlation matrix (Matrix::nearPD(corr=TRUE) in R). Use with care (default False).

    		 False
    sparse bool

    Return a sparse matrix (default False).

    		 False
    retdat bool

    Return a data frame of the variables used with the matrix appended in columns V.1, V.2, ... instead of the matrix (default False; metafor takes this as an undocumented extra argument).

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    NDArray[float64] | csr_array | DataFrame

    The k x k variance-covariance matrix, with k the length of vi: a dense array that prints like metafor's vcovmat
    NDArray[float64] | csr_array | DataFrame

    (VCovMat), a scipy.sparse.csr_array if sparse=True, or with retdat=True a data frame of
    NDArray[float64] | csr_array | DataFrame

    the variables used with the matrix in the columns V.1, V.2, ....

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    an argument or the data is invalid (R stops with an error here).
    NotFoundError

    a named column is not in data.
    ArgumentError

    rho has an unsupported type.
    Metafor reference

    rcalc ¶

    rcalc(
    x: str
    | (NDArray[float64] | DataFrame)
    | Sequence[NDArray[float64] | DataFrame]
    | Mapping[str, NDArray[float64] | DataFrame],
    ni: ArrayLike | str | None | float = None,
    data: DataFrame | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    rtoz: bool = False,
    nfun: str | Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float] = 'min',
    sparse: bool = False,
    upper: bool = False,
    simplify: bool = True,
    *,
    rowid: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    vnames: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    noid: bool | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> RCalcResult | dict[str, RCalcResult]

    Variance-covariance matrix of correlation coefficients from the same samples (metafor's rcalc).

    Correlations computed from the same sample are not independent. Equations for the sampling covariances can be found in Steiger (1980, doi:10.1037/0033-2909.87.2.245) and Olkin and Finn (1990, doi:10.1037/0033-2909.108.2.330); for raw correlations the denominator is ni - 1 (as in metafor), for r-to-z transformed ones ni - 3. The data and the matrix can be passed on to rma_mv. As in R, the study identifier in dat consists of strings (the names of the list, or the ids converted to character).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x str | (NDArray[float64] | DataFrame) | Sequence[NDArray[float64] | DataFrame] | Mapping[str, NDArray[float64] | DataFrame]

    A formula string such as 'ri ~ var1 + var2 | study' (the study part may be left out for a single study), naming the correlations, the two variables of each and the study in data; or a correlation matrix; or a list or dict of correlation matrices. Matrices are arrays or data frames whose column labels name the variables (x1, x2, ... if unnamed).

    		 required
    ni ArrayLike | str | None | float

    Sample sizes the correlations are based on: for a formula, a column name of data or an array; for a matrix, the (common) sample size; for a list of matrices, one sample size per matrix. Required.

    		 None
    data DataFrame | Mapping[str, Any] | None

    Data frame (or mapping of columns) holding the variables of the formula (and ni). Required for a formula.

    		 None
    rtoz bool

    Transform the correlations with Fisher's r-to-z transformation and compute the matrix for the transformed values (default False).

    		 False
    nfun str | Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]

    How the common sample size within a study is computed when it differs between correlations: 'min' (the default; conservative), 'harmonic' (harmonic mean) or 'mean', an unambiguous prefix of these, or a function of the array of the sample sizes of a study returning a single value.

    		 'min'
    sparse bool

    Return the matrix as a sparse matrix (default False; only with a list of matrices or a formula does this give a sparse V).

    		 False
    upper bool

    For matrices, use the upper instead of the lower triangle (default False; metafor takes this as an undocumented extra argument).

    		 False
    simplify bool

    For a list of matrices, combine the results into one (default True); with False a dict of one result per matrix (metafor takes this as an undocumented extra argument).

    		 True
    rowid Sequence[str] | None

    For a list of matrices with simplify=True: values of 'id.var1.var2' giving the order of the rows of dat and V (metafor passes this on internally for a formula).

    		 None
    vnames Sequence[str] | None

    For a list of matrices with simplify=True: four names for the columns of dat.

    		 None
    noid bool | None

    For a list of matrices with simplify=True: drop the study identifier from dat (default False).

    		 None
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    Stands for R's options(na.action=); an unknown value raises, the known ones ('omit' (the default), 'exclude', 'pass' and 'fail') give the same result (metafor sets na.pass while it computes).

    		 'omit'

    Returns:

    Type Description
    RCalcResult | dict[str, RCalcResult]

    An RCalcResult with the data dat (one row per correlation) and the block diagonal variance-covariance matrix
    RCalcResult | dict[str, RCalcResult]

    V. A covariance is NaN when a correlation it needs is missing, and nothing is computed for studies with a common sample size
    RCalcResult | dict[str, RCalcResult]

    below 5. With simplify=False and a list of matrices, a dict of one such result per matrix.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ArgumentError

    x is not a formula, a matrix or a list of matrices.
    InputError

    an argument or the data is invalid (R stops with an error here).
    NotFoundError

    a variable of the formula is not in data.
    Metafor reference

    rcalc

    RCalcResult dataclass ¶

    RCalcResult(
    dat: DataFrame | None, V: FloatArray | csr_array | None
)

    The pair of dat (one row per correlation) and V (their variance-covariance matrix) that rcalc returns.

    Both are None for a single matrix of dimension 1 x 1 or smaller. V is dense, except that sparse=True with a list of matrices (or a formula) gives a scipy.sparse.csr_array.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    dat DataFrame | None

    Data frame with one row per correlation, with the columns var1 and var2 (the two variable identifiers), var1.var2 (a variable pair identifier), yi (the correlation, possibly r-to-z transformed) and ni (the common sample size). For a list of matrices (and so for a formula) it has the study identifier as its first column (id, or the name of the study variable of a formula).
    V FloatArray | csr_array | None

    The block diagonal variance-covariance matrix of the correlations; its row and column names are in dat['var1.var2'].

    bldiag ¶

    bldiag(
    *mlist: ArrayLike
    | DataFrame
    | sparray
    | spmatrix
    | Mapping[
        Any, ArrayLike | DataFrame | sparray | spmatrix
    ],
    order: ArrayLike | None = None,
    order_is_permutation: bool = False,
) -> NDArray[float64]

    Block diagonal matrix from matrices (metafor's bldiag).

    Accepts matrices (arrays, data frames or scipy sparse arrays), vectors and scalars (turned into diagonal matrices, so bldiag(numpy.ones((3, 3)), 2) works) or a single list, tuple or dict (R's named list) of these. Matrices with zero rows or columns are dropped; if none are left the result is 0 x 0.

    order is the clustering variable according to which the rows and columns of the result are reordered back to the original order of the data (R: order=cluster). With order_is_permutation=True it is instead the permutation itself (R: order=order(cluster)).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    *mlist ArrayLike | DataFrame | sparray | spmatrix | Mapping[Any, ArrayLike | DataFrame | sparray | spmatrix]

    The matrices to put on the diagonal: arrays, data frames or scipy sparse arrays, vectors and scalars (made diagonal), or a single list, tuple or dict of these.

    		 ()
    order ArrayLike | None

    Clustering variable (one value per row of the result) used to reorder the rows and columns of a square result back to the original order of the data, for blocks that were built in the order of the sorted clusters. None (the default) keeps the order of the blocks.

    		 None
    order_is_permutation bool

    Treat order as the permutation itself (R's order=order(cluster)) rather than as a clustering variable (default False).

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    NDArray[float64]

    The block diagonal matrix, a dense array (0 x 0 if no non-empty matrices were given). Unlike metafor, which gives the result the class
    NDArray[float64]

    vcovmat when an element has it, the result is a plain array.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    order is used with a non-square result or has the wrong length.
    ArgumentError

    an element is an array with more than two dimensions.
    ValueError

    an element cannot be converted to numbers (raised by NumPy).

    blsplit ¶

    blsplit(
    x: NDArray[float64] | sparray | spmatrix,
    cluster: ArrayLike,
    fun: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    args: Any = None,

) -> dict[Any, Any]

    Split a block diagonal matrix into a dict of sub-matrices, one per unique cluster value (metafor's blsplit).

    The keys are the unique cluster values in order of appearance (sorted if sort). fun, if given, is applied to each sub-matrix with args as additional positional arguments, i.e. fun(block, *args) (R: blsplit(V, cluster, round, 4); a single value is the one argument). A scipy sparse x gives sparse sub-matrices.

    A symmetric block diagonal matrix, a dense array or a scipy sparse array.

    		 required
    cluster ArrayLike

    Clustering variable to split by, with one value per row of x.

    		 required
    fun Callable[..., Any] | None

    A function applied to each sub-matrix (for example round). None (the default) returns the sub-matrices unchanged.

    		 None
    args Any

    Additional positional argument(s) for fun, given as fun(block, *args); a single value is the one argument.

    		 None
    sort bool

    Sort the result by the unique values of cluster instead of their order of appearance (default False).

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    dict[Any, Any]

    A dict (a NamedList) of the sub-matrices (after fun) keyed by the unique values of cluster.

    x is not a matrix.

    Rows contrast each pair of the coefficients picked by btt (0-based, or a regex).

    For use as anova(res, X=pairmat(res, btt='alloc')), or without the model, anova(res, X=pairmat(btt='alloc')), as in metafor, where the model is that of the anova() or predict() call. Rows for the coefficients picked by btt2 themselves are placed first. fixed=True matches a string btt or btt2 literally instead of as a regular expression (metafor's ... argument). The contrast matrix can be passed to anova (to test the contrasts) and predict (for their confidence intervals).

    Regression on correlation and covariance matrices¶

    matreg ¶

    matreg(
    y: int | str,
    x: Sequence[int | str] | int | str | None = None,
    R: ArrayLike | DataFrame | None = None,
    n: float | None = None,
    V: ArrayLike | DataFrame | None = None,
    cov: bool = False,
    means: ArrayLike | None = None,
    ztor: bool = False,
    nearpd: bool = False,
    level: float = 95,
    digits: int | None = None,
) -> MatregResult

    Fit a regression model to a correlation or covariance matrix (metafor's matreg).

    y is the outcome: a 0-based index into R, a variable name (R must then be a frame with dimension names) or a formula string such as 'perf ~ acog + asom + conf' (which also gives x). x are the predictors (indices or names; by default every other variable). Give either n, the sample size the matrix is based on, or V, the variance-covariance matrix of the elements of the lower triangle of R (column-wise, with the diagonal when cov=True), for instance from :func:metafopy.rcalc or the vcov() of a multivariate model of correlations. cov=True treats R as a covariance matrix (the model then has an intercept, which needs means), ztor=True back-transforms Fisher r-to-z transformed correlations (and their V) and nearpd=True replaces a non-positive-definite R[x, x] by the nearest correlation matrix (:func:metafopy.core.linalg.near_pd, a port of Matrix::nearPD).

    Without names, the coefficients are labelled x1, x2, ... by their 1-based position in R, as in R.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    y int | str

    The outcome variable: a 0-based index into R, a variable name (R must then be a data frame with dimension names) or a formula string such as 'perf ~ acog + asom + conf', which also gives x.

    		 required
    x Sequence[int | str] | int | str | None

    The predictor variables: a sequence of 0-based indices or names (or a single one). Ignored when y is a formula. None (the default) uses every variable other than y.

    		 None
    R ArrayLike | DataFrame | None

    The correlation or covariance matrix (an array or data frame; required). Only its lower triangle (including the diagonal) is used.

    		 None
    n float | None

    The sample size the matrix is based on; gives the standard errors of a regression on raw data (t tests). Give n or V, not both.

    		 None
    V ArrayLike | DataFrame | None

    The variance-covariance matrix of the elements of the lower triangle of R, column-wise (with the diagonal when cov=True), for instance from rcalc or the vcov() of a multivariate model of correlations. Gives the standard errors by the multivariate delta method (z tests). Give n or V, not both.

    		 None
    cov bool

    Treat R as a covariance matrix; the model then has an intercept, which needs means (default False, a correlation matrix).

    		 False
    means ArrayLike | None

    The means of the variables, for the intercept when cov=True. Without them the intercept estimate is NaN.

    		 None
    ztor bool

    R (and V) hold Fisher r-to-z transformed correlations, which are back-transformed to raw correlations first (default False).

    		 False
    nearpd bool

    Replace an R[x, x] that cannot be inverted (is not positive definite) by the nearest correlation matrix (a port of Matrix::nearPD) instead of failing (default False). Treat the results with caution. metafor's undocumented nearPD alias of this argument is not accepted.

    		 False
    level float

    Confidence interval level in percent (default 95), or a value below 1 read as in metafor.

    		 95
    digits int | None

    Number of decimals used when the result is printed (default 4).

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    MatregResult

    A MatregResult: the table tab of (standardised, for a correlation matrix) regression coefficients with
    MatregResult

    their standard errors, test statistics, p-values and confidence interval bounds, the variance-covariance matrix vb of the
    MatregResult

    coefficients, R2 and further fit statistics. It has coef, vcov, confint and predict methods.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    an argument is missing, invalid or inconsistent with R.
    ArgumentError

    a logical argument is not a bool.
    EstimationError

    R[x, x] cannot be inverted, or n does not exceed the number of regression coefficients.
    Metafor reference

    matreg

    tab: DataFrame,

    R2: float,
    p: int,
    parms: int,
    digits: int,
    test: Literal['t', 'z'],
    level: float,
    intercept: bool,
    R2adj: float | None = None,
    F: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None,
    Fdf: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    Fp: float | None = None,
    df_residual: float | None = None,

    QMdf: tuple[int, None] | None = None,
    QMp: float | None = None,
)

    A regression model fitted to a correlation or covariance matrix (metafor's matreg object).

    tab holds the columns beta, se, tval and df (test == 't', a model fitted with n) or zval (test == 'z', a model fitted with V), pval, ci.lb and ci.ub. The F test (F, Fdf, Fp), R2adj, the residual variances and fit_stats exist only for test == 't'; the Wald test (QM, QMdf, QMp) only for test == 'z'. level is the alpha level (0.05 for 95%) and intercept is true for a covariance matrix input (cov=True).

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    tab DataFrame

    Table of coefficients, one row per coefficient (see above for the columns).
    vb DataFrame

    Variance-covariance matrix of the coefficients.
    R2 float

    Proportion of variance of the outcome explained by the predictors.
    p int

    Number of estimated coefficients for a model fitted with n (the intercept included when cov=True); the number of predictors for a model fitted with V.
    parms int

    Number of estimated parameters: p + 1 for a model fitted with n (the residual variance counts), p for one fitted with V.
    digits int

    Number of decimals used when the result is printed.
    test Literal['t', 'z']

    't' for a model fitted with n, 'z' for one fitted with V.
    level float

    The alpha level of the confidence intervals.
    intercept bool

    Whether the model has an intercept.
    R2adj float | None

    Adjusted R^2 (test == 't' only).
    F tuple[float, float, float] | None

    The F test of the predictors as a tuple (statistic, numerator degrees of freedom, denominator degrees of freedom) (test == 't' only).
    Fdf tuple[float, float] | None

    Degrees of freedom of the F test (test == 't' only).
    Fp float | None

    P-value of the F test (test == 't' only).
    df_residual float | None

    Residual degrees of freedom (test == 't' only).
    sigma2_ml float | None

    Maximum-likelihood estimate of the residual variance (test == 't' only).
    sigma2_reml float | None

    Restricted maximum-likelihood estimate of the residual variance (test == 't' only).
    nobs float | None

    Number of observations (test == 't' only).
    deviance float | None

    Deviance of the model (test == 't' only).
    fit_stats DataFrame | None

    Log-likelihood, deviance, AIC, BIC and AICc under ML and REML (test == 't' only).
    QM float | None

    Wald-type test statistic of the coefficients (test == 'z' only).
    QMdf tuple[int, None] | None

    Degrees of freedom of the Wald test (test == 'z' only).
    QMp float | None

    P-value of the Wald test (test == 'z' only).

    Bases: PredictResult

    Predicted values of a matreg fit (predict.matreg), without prediction intervals (pi_lb and pi_ub are NaN).

    X is the matrix of predictor values (addx=True), vcov the variance-covariance matrix of the predicted values (vcov=True without transf), ddf the degrees of freedom of the t-distribution (None for a model fitted with V) and transf whether a transformation was applied (se is then NaN, as in metafor).

    The attributes pred, se, ci_lb, ci_ub, pi_lb and pi_ub are those of the predict result.

    Estimated marginal means¶

    emmprep ¶

    emmprep(
    x: RMAResult
    | RMAMVResult
    | GLMMResult
    | FixedBinaryResult
    | RMALSResult
    | SelmodelResult,
    verbose: bool = False,
    *,
    data: DataFrame | None = None,
    df: float | None = None,
    sigma: float | None = None,
    tran: Link | str | None = None,
    at: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    cov_reduce: Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]
    | Mapping[str, Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]]
    | None = None,
    nesting: str
    | Mapping[str, str | Sequence[str]]
    | None
    | Literal['auto'] = 'auto',
) -> EmmGrid

    Prepare a reference grid from a fitted model, as metafor's emmprep does for emmeans' qdrg.

    The grid has one row per combination of the levels of the factors in the model formula, with each numeric predictor at its mean over the studies (cov_reduce) or at the values given in at. Pass the grid to emmeans (and then to contrast, pairs and regrid) to get estimated marginal means. When the model knows its effect size measure, the back-transformation (for example exponentiation for log ratios) is stored in the grid and applied by type='response'.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x RMAResult | RMAMVResult | GLMMResult | FixedBinaryResult | RMALSResult | SelmodelResult

    A fitted model with a formula: a model from rma_uni, rma_mv, rma_glmm, rma_mh or rma_peto, a location-scale model or a selection model. Models with redundant predictors that were dropped cannot be used.

    		 required
    verbose bool

    Print the extracted formula, degrees of freedom, tau^2 and transformation (default False).

    		 False
    data DataFrame | None

    Data frame with the variables of the model, to build the grid from instead of the data used in the fit. None (the default) uses the data of the fit.

    		 None
    df float | None

    Degrees of freedom of the tests and intervals. None (the default) takes them from the fit (the smallest ddf; infinite for z tests).

    		 None
    sigma float | None

    Error standard deviation used for bias adjustment in back-transformations (the square root of tau^2). None (the default) takes it from the fit, or 0 for rma_mv and location-scale fits, where it cannot be extracted.

    		 None
    tran Link | str | None

    Transformation of the estimates, a link object or its name (for example 'log' or 'logit'), or 'none' for none. As in emmeans, a name that is no known transformation gives the identity link carrying that name; '+.sqrt' is not supported. None (the default) derives it from the effect size measure ('log' for ratio measures, 'logit' for PLO, and so on).

    		 None
    at Mapping[str, Any] | None

    Mapping from variable names to the values to use in the grid: for a numeric predictor its values instead of its mean, for a factor a subset of its levels. Other variables are as by default.

    		 None
    cov_reduce Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float] | Mapping[str, Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]] | None

    Function reducing the values of a numeric predictor to the one used in the grid, or a mapping from variable names to such functions. None (the default) uses the mean.

    		 None
    nesting str | Mapping[str, str | Sequence[str]] | None | Literal['auto']

    Factors nested in others, as text such as 'grp %in% lat' (several separated by commas) or a mapping from each nested factor to the factor(s) it is nested in. 'auto' (the default) detects the nesting from the combinations of levels in the data and the terms of the model (lat + lat:grp nests grp in lat); None switches the detection off. Combinations that cannot occur are hidden and left out of the means.

    		 'auto'

    Returns:

    Type Description
    EmmGrid

    An EmmGrid: the reference grid, with the coefficients and their variance-covariance matrix, the degrees of freedom
    EmmGrid

    and the transformation stored.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ArgumentError

    x is not a fitted model of a supported class.
    InputError

    the fit cannot be used (redundant predictors, no formula or data) or an argument is invalid.
    NotSupportedError

    tran is '+.sqrt'.

    emmeans ¶

    emmeans(
    object: EmmGrid
    | (
        RMAResult
        | RMAMVResult
        | GLMMResult
        | FixedBinaryResult
        | RMALSResult
        | SelmodelResult
    ),
    specs: str | Sequence[str],
    by: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    *,
    weights: str
    | Sequence[float]
    | Sequence[Sequence[float]]
    | NDArray[float64] = 'equal',
    at: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    cov_reduce: Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]
    | Mapping[str, Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]]
    | None = None,
    null: float | None = None,
    delta: float | None = None,
    side: int | float | str | None = None,
    type: str | None = None,
    **prep: Any,
) -> EmmGrid

    Estimated marginal means: the reference grid averaged over the variables not named in specs (and by).

    object is a reference grid from :func:emmprep or a fit (at, cov_reduce and further keywords then go to :func:emmprep). specs names the variables ('alloc', ['alloc', 'lat'] or an R-style '~ alloc | lat'; '1' or '~ 1' for the overall mean) and by the variables the results are grouped by. weights averages over the other factors with 'equal' weights, 'proportional' (frequencies in the data), 'outer' (products of the marginal frequencies), 'cells' or 'flat' (cell frequencies, the latter ignoring empty cells), a vector with one weight per combination of those factors, or a matrix whose columns are those combinations and whose rows are the weights of the successive means (recycled when there are more means than rows).

    With nested factors (see :func:emmprep) the means of a nested factor are given within the groups it is nested in, and the other factors are averaged over the combinations that occur in the data. null, delta and side set the defaults of the tests of :meth:EmmGrid.summary; so does type ('response' shows the back-transformed means by default, as emmeans(..., type='response')). See https://rvlenth.github.io/emmeans/reference/emmeans.html.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    object EmmGrid | (RMAResult | RMAMVResult | GLMMResult | FixedBinaryResult | RMALSResult | SelmodelResult)

    A reference grid from emmprep, or a fitted model (see emmprep for the classes), for which a grid is made first.

    		 required
    specs str | Sequence[str]

    The variables to get means for: a name, a sequence of names, or an R-style formula such as '~ alloc | lat'; '1' or '~ 1' for the overall mean.

    		 required
    by str | Sequence[str] | None

    Variables the results are grouped by. None (the default) for none (or those after | in specs).

    		 None
    weights str | Sequence[float] | Sequence[Sequence[float]] | NDArray[float64]

    How the other factors are averaged over (a string may be abbreviated, for example 'prop'): 'equal' (the default), 'proportional' (frequencies in the data), 'outer' (products of the marginal frequencies), 'cells' or 'flat' (cell frequencies, the latter ignoring empty cells), a vector with one weight per combination of those factors, or a matrix whose columns are those combinations and whose rows are the weights of the successive means (recycled when there are more means than rows).

    		 'equal'
    at Mapping[str, Any] | None

    Mapping from variable names to the values of the grid (see emmprep); only when object is a fitted model.

    		 None
    cov_reduce Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float] | Mapping[str, Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]] | None

    Reduction of the numeric predictors (see emmprep); only when object is a fitted model.

    		 None
    null float | None

    Value the tests of the summary compare the estimates with. None keeps the value of the grid (default 0).

    		 None
    delta float | None

    Threshold of equivalence and non-inferiority tests of the summary. None keeps the value of the grid (default 0).

    		 None
    side int | float | str | None

    Tail of the tests of the summary: -1, 0 or 1 (or '<', '!=', '>', or a word such as 'left', 'both', 'right', 'noninferiority', 'equivalence'). None keeps the value of the grid (default both sides).

    		 None
    type str | None

    Default scale of summaries: 'link' (the transformed scale) or 'response' (back-transformed). None (the default) keeps the default of the grid.

    		 None
    **prep Any

    Further keywords for emmprep (verbose, data, df, sigma, tran, nesting); only when object is a fitted model.

    		 {}

    Returns:

    Type Description
    EmmGrid

    An EmmGrid of the estimated marginal means (with summary() to get the table).

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    a variable is not in the grid, the weights do not fit the averaged factors, type is not 'link' or 'response', or at, cov_reduce or other emmprep keywords are given with a reference grid.

    contrast ¶

    contrast(
    object: EmmGrid,
    method: str | Mapping[str, Sequence[float]] = 'eff',
    *,
    by: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    interaction: bool | str | Sequence[str] = False,
    name: str = 'contrast',
    adjust: str | None = None,
    ref: int | str | Sequence[int | str] | None = None,
    exclude: int | str | Sequence[int | str] | None = None,
    include: int | str | Sequence[int | str] | None = None,
    reverse: bool = False,
    wts: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    max_degree: int | None = None,
    enhance_levels: bool = True,
    null: float | None = None,
    delta: float | None = None,
    side: int | float | str | None = None,
) -> EmmGrid

    Contrasts of the estimates of a reference grid or of marginal means (emmeans' contrast).

    method is one of :data:metafopy.methods.emm_contrasts.METHODS ('pairwise', 'revpairwise', 'trt_vs_ctrl', 'trt_vs_ctrlk', 'dunnett', 'eff', 'del_eff', 'consec', 'mean_chg', 'poly', 'identity') or a mapping from contrast names to coefficient vectors, one per row of the grid. The contrasts are formed separately for each combination of the by variables (those of object by default). ref, exclude and include are 0-based indices or level labels. With interaction (True for method on every factor, or one method per factor) contrasts of contrasts are formed, one per combination of the factors. null, delta and side set the defaults of the tests of :meth:EmmGrid.summary.

    With nested factors the contrasts are formed within each combination of the groups in by (those a nested factor is nested in are added to it), and the groups can differ in size; only the named methods can be used then. See https://rvlenth.github.io/emmeans/reference/contrast.html.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    object EmmGrid

    A reference grid or marginal means (EmmGrid).

    		 required
    method str | Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]

    The contrasts: the name of a method ('pairwise', 'revpairwise', 'tukey', 'trt_vs_ctrl', 'trt_vs_ctrl1', 'trt_vs_ctrlk', 'dunnett', 'eff' (the default), 'del_eff', 'consec', 'mean_chg', 'poly' or 'identity'), or a mapping from contrast names to coefficient vectors with one value per row of the grid (per group).

    		 'eff'
    by str | Sequence[str] | None

    Variables to form the contrasts within. None (the default) uses those of object.

    		 None
    interaction bool | str | Sequence[str]

    False (the default) for ordinary contrasts. True forms contrasts of contrasts, applying method to every factor, and a name or sequence of names gives the method for each factor; one contrast per combination of the factors results.

    		 False
    name str

    Name of the column of the contrasts (default 'contrast').

    		 'contrast'
    adjust str | None

    Multiplicity adjustment stored in the result for its tests and intervals: 'tukey', 'scheffe', 'sidak', 'dunnettx', 'mvt', 'holm', 'hochberg', 'hommel', 'bonferroni', 'BH', 'BY', 'fdr' or 'none'. None (the default) uses the default of the method (for example 'tukey' for 'pairwise'). As in emmeans, 'tukey', 'scheffe' and 'dunnettx' apply to two-sided tests only, and the methods of p.adjust ('holm' to 'fdr') to tests, not intervals (which then use 'bonferroni').

    		 None
    ref int | str | Sequence[int | str] | None

    The reference level(s) of 'trt_vs_ctrl' and similar methods: 0-based indices or level labels. Default the first level.

    		 None
    exclude int | str | Sequence[int | str] | None

    Levels left out of the contrasts: 0-based indices or level labels.

    		 None
    include int | str | Sequence[int | str] | None

    Levels to use in the contrasts (the others are left out): 0-based indices or level labels.

    		 None
    reverse bool

    Reverse the direction of the contrasts, for example later minus earlier (default False).

    		 False
    wts Sequence[float] | None

    Weights of the levels for the 'eff' and 'del_eff' methods, normalised to sum to 1: one value per level, or per included level when exclude or include is used. None (the default) for equal weights. emmeans' wts = NA (take the weights from the grid) is not supported.

    		 None
    max_degree int | None

    Maximum degree of the 'poly' contrasts (at most 20). None (the default) for min(6, k - 1) with k levels, as the max.degree default of emmeans' poly.emmc.

    		 None
    enhance_levels bool

    Put the variable name in front of numeric levels in the labels of the contrasts (default True).

    		 True
    null float | None

    Value the tests of the summary compare the estimates with. None keeps the value of the grid (default 0).

    		 None
    delta float | None

    Threshold of equivalence and non-inferiority tests of the summary. None keeps the value of the grid (default 0).

    		 None
    side int | float | str | None

    Tail of the tests of the summary: -1, 0 or 1 (or '<', '!=', '>', or a word such as 'left', 'both', 'right', 'noninferiority', 'equivalence'). None keeps the value of the grid (default both sides).

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    EmmGrid

    An EmmGrid of the contrasts, with one row per contrast.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    the method or an argument does not fit the grid.

    regrid ¶

    regrid(
    object: EmmGrid,
    *,
    bias_adjust: bool = False,
    sigma: float | None = None,
) -> EmmGrid

    Back-transform the estimates, so that later contrasts are of the back-transformed values (emmeans' regrid).

    The variance-covariance matrix of the transformed estimates follows by the delta method. Without a transformation the grid is returned as is, with an identity linfct. Only the default transform = 'response' of emmeans is available: there are no transform, inv_link_lbl, predict_type, N_sim or sim arguments. See https://rvlenth.github.io/emmeans/reference/regrid.html.

    Error standard deviation for the bias adjustment. None (the default) uses the one stored in the grid.

    		 None

    EmmGrid dataclass ¶

    EmmGrid(
    grid: DataFrame,
    levels: dict[str, tuple[Any, ...]],
    numeric: tuple[str, ...],
    linfct: FloatArray,
    bhat: FloatArray,
    vb: FloatArray,
    df: float,
    wgt: FloatArray | None,
    est_name: str,
    est_type: str,
    by: tuple[str, ...],
    adjust: str,
    fam_size: int,
    infer: tuple[bool, bool],
    link: Link | None,
    inv_label: str | None,
    log_contrast: bool,
    sigma: float | None,
    avgd_over: tuple[str, ...],
    messages: tuple[str, ...],
    pairby: tuple[str, ...] | None,
    pri_vars: tuple[str, ...],
    level: float = 0.95,
    measure: str = 'GEN',
    nesting: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = dict(),
    display: tuple[bool, ...] | None = None,
    avgd_qualifier: str = '',
    null: float = 0.0,
    delta: float = 0.0,
    side: int = 0,
    summary_type: str | None = None,
)

    A reference grid, a set of estimated marginal means, or contrasts of them (emmeans' emmGrid).

    grid has one row per estimate and one column per variable; the estimates are linfct @ bhat with the variance-covariance matrix linfct @ vb @ linfct.T and degrees of freedom df (infinite for z tests). wgt holds the number of studies behind each row of a reference grid, which the weights of :func:emmeans use. link is the transformation of the estimates (type='response' of :meth:summary back-transforms them), inv_label the name of the back-transformed estimate and sigma the error SD used for the bias adjustment. nesting maps each nested factor to the factors it is nested in, and display marks the rows of the grid that occur (the others are hidden from summaries and left out of the averages). null, delta and side are the defaults of the tests of :meth:summary, summary_type the default type.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description

    Data frame with one row per estimate and one column per variable.
    levels dict[str, tuple[Any, ...]]

    The levels of each factor, by variable name.
    numeric tuple[str, ...]

    linfct FloatArray

    Matrix of linear functions: each row gives an estimate as a combination of the model coefficients bhat.
    bhat FloatArray

    The model coefficients.
    vb FloatArray

    Variance-covariance matrix of the model coefficients.
    df float

    Degrees of freedom of the tests and intervals (infinite for z tests).
    wgt FloatArray | None

    Number of studies behind each row of a reference grid, used by proportional weights, or None.
    est_name str

    Name of the estimate column in summaries (for example 'prediction', 'emmean' or 'estimate').
    est_type str

    What the estimates are (for example 'prediction').
    by tuple[str, ...]

    Variables the results are grouped by.
    adjust str

    Multiplicity adjustment of the tests and intervals.
    fam_size int

    Number of estimates in a family, used by the adjustments.
    infer tuple[bool, bool]

    Whether summaries give confidence intervals and tests, as a pair.
    link Link | None

    Transformation of the estimates, or None.
    inv_label str | None

    Name of the back-transformed estimate, or None.
    log_contrast bool

    Whether the contrasts are of log-scale estimates (so back-transformed they are ratios).
    sigma float | None

    Error SD used for the bias adjustment, or None.
    avgd_over tuple[str, ...]

    Variables the estimates are averaged over.
    messages tuple[str, ...]

    Notes printed under summaries.
    pairby tuple[str, ...] | None

    Variables of a pairwise grouping, or None.
    pri_vars tuple[str, ...]

    Names of the primary variables.
    level float

    Confidence level of the intervals (default 0.95).
    measure str

    The effect size measure of the model.
    nesting dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]

    Maps each nested factor to the factors it is nested in.
    display tuple[bool, ...] | None

    Qualifier printed in the note about the averaging.

    delta float

    Default threshold of equivalence tests.
    side int

    Default tail of the tests (-1, 0 or 1).
    summary_type str | None

    Default type of summaries ('link' or 'response'), or None.

    Random number generator¶

    set_seed ¶

    set_seed(seed: int) -> RRandom

    Seed the module-level random number generator (R's set.seed()).

    The generator reproduces R's default Mersenne-Twister with rejection sampling. The functions that draw random numbers when they are given no seed or rng use this generator: among them permutest, gosh (with random subsets), hettest (the bootstrap), vif (with sim=True), fsn (with exact=True), qqnorm (the envelope) and conv_fivenum (methods 'bc' and 'mln'). After set_seed(s) the results of permutest, gosh, hettest, vif and conv_fivenum were compared with those of metafor after set.seed(s) and agree. Without a call the generator is seeded from the clock on first use.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    seed int

    The integer seed, as given to R's set.seed().

    		 required

    Returns:

    Type Description
    RRandom

    The new generator, an RRandom that can also be passed to functions that take an rng argument.
